html:
Request for Proposal (RFP)
Supply of Hardware Materials, Solar System, Fixtures & Ancillary Items for Construction of Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre at Hillary Park, Maneybung GPU, West Sikkim
Ref. No.: PPHF/5031/26-27/Cafeteria Materials Hillary Park
Date: 30th September 2026

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF), New Delhi, invites sealed/digital quotations under a Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) for the Supply of Hardware Materials, Solar System, Fixtures & Ancillary Items for Construction of Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre at Hillary Park / Tenzing Hillary Park, Maneybung GPU, West Sikkim (Financial Year 2026–2027) as per the specifications and requirements detailed below.

RFP Details

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5031/26-27/Cafeteria Materials Hillary Park
Date of Issue of RFP30th September 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission5th October 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs6th October 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected Financial Bid)

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible authorised dealers, suppliers, hardware merchants, solar solution providers and registered vendors for the supply and delivery of hardware materials, off-grid rooftop solar system, water purifier, branding/signage, umbrella banks, Wi-Fi connectivity and related items for the ongoing construction of Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre at Hillary Park (Tenzing Hillary Park), Maneybung GPU, Gyalshing District, West Sikkim under the PPHF component of the convergence project.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

The construction of Cafeteria cum Organic and Rural Artisan Marketing Centre near Tenzing Hillary Park, Maneybung GPU (Ward: Gumapadara / Sangdara), West Sikkim has been sanctioned in convergence with MGNREGA / VB-G RAM-G, GPDP, MPLADS and PPHF under HRDD-HDFC CSR initiative. The civil construction work is in the verge of completion. As per the requisitions issued by the Additional District Collector (Development), Gyalshing (Memo dated 22/09/2026 and 30/07/2026), specific hardware materials and non-civil items are required to be supplied by PPHF so that the asset can be completed and handed over without further delay.

2.2 Purpose

The purpose of this RFP is to select a competent, authorised supplier/dealer for the timely supply and site delivery of the listed materials (hardware, solar power system, water purifier, branding, umbrella banks and Wi-Fi) strictly as per the approved specifications and brands.

2.3 Objectives

  • To procure and supply quality-assured hardware materials (GCI sheets, steel bars, bricks, nails, cutter blades, mangara) of specified brands and sizes.
  • To supply, install (where applicable) and commission a 2 kW off-grid rooftop solar system complete with panels, inverter and batteries.
  • To supply and install Hot & Cold Water Purifier, customised branding & radium signage (3 sides), Umbrella Bank (20 Nos.) and Wi-Fi connectivity with 6-month subscription.
  • To ensure delivery at the project site (Hillary Park / Maneybung GPU) and handover to the Panchayat President with proper challan and tax invoice.
  • To complete the supply within the stipulated timeline so that the Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre can be made fully functional.

2.4 Targeted Beneficiaries

Direct Beneficiaries: Local artisans, SHG members, farmers, youth and community members of Maneybung GPU and surrounding villages who will utilise the Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre for livelihood and marketing of organic/rural products.

Indirect Beneficiaries: Tourists visiting Tenzing Hillary Park / Uttarey area, local administration and Panchayat institutions through improved community infrastructure.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/supplier will be responsible for the end-to-end supply, transportation, unloading and delivery of the following materials at the project site located at Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre, Hillary Park / Tenzing Hillary Park, Maneybung GPU, Gyalshing District, West Sikkim. All materials shall conform to the brands/makes and specifications indicated. Installation support for solar system, water purifier, branding and Wi-Fi shall be provided as required.

3.1 Bill of Materials (Hardware & Construction Items)

4Iron Steel Bar 1.5 inchDurgapur Steel / EquivalentNos.60

3.3 Off-Grid Rooftop Solar System (2 kW)

Complete system comprising:

S.NoComponentPreferred Brand / MakeUnitQty

13bOff-Grid Inverter – 3 kWMicrotek / EquivalentNos.1
13cLead Acid Battery – 200 AhExide / Microtek / LuminousNos.2

The solar system shall be complete with all necessary mounting structure, cables, MCBs, earthing and installation at the site so as to power the market / cafeteria facilities.

3.4 Delivery & Handover Requirements

  • All materials shall be delivered at the project site (Cafeteria cum Rural Artisan Marketing Centre, Hillary Park / Maneybung GPU).
  • Materials shall be handed over to the Panchayat President, Maneybung GPU with proper delivery challan and tax invoice.
  • Copy of challan / invoice shall be submitted to the Project Manager, PPHF and ADC (Development), Gyalshing.
  • Solar system, water purifier, branding and Wi-Fi shall include basic installation and commissioning support.
  • All materials must be new, unused and of the specified brands or approved equivalent (with prior written approval of PPHF).

4. Timeline

The entire supply and delivery (including installation of solar, purifier, branding and Wi-Fi) shall be completed within 21 (twenty-one) days from the date of the Work Order / Purchase Order. A detailed delivery schedule shall be submitted with the Technical Proposal.

5. Applicable Indian Compliance & Statutory Acts

Bidders must ensure all supply, materials, documentation and process workflows strictly comply with the following:

  • Relevant BIS / ISI standards for steel, GCI sheets, bricks, solar panels, batteries, inverters and electrical fittings.
  • GST & Tax Regulations: CGST and SGST compliance with valid GSTIN; tax invoices mandatory.
  • MSMED Act, 2006: Benefits applicable to registered MSMEs.
  • Environmental norms for packaging and disposal of packaging waste.
  • Any applicable State (Sikkim) regulations for transportation of construction materials.

6. Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for evaluation, a Bidder must satisfy all the following minimum eligibility conditions and furnish documentary proof in the Technical Bid:

  1. The Bidder shall be a legally constituted entity (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company or registered dealer/supplier) operating in India.
  2. The Bidder shall hold a valid Trade Licence / Dealership Certificate and a valid GST Registration Certificate.
  3. The Bidder shall hold a valid PAN issued by the Income-tax Department.
  4. The Bidder should be an authorised dealer / stockist of the preferred brands (JSW / TATA / Durgapur Steel / Aquaguard / Waaree / Microtek / Exide etc.) or able to supply genuine products of these brands with supporting authorisation / invoice trail.
  5. The Bidder should have satisfactorily executed similar supply orders of construction hardware / solar systems / institutional materials during the last three (03) financial years (supported by work orders / invoices).
  6. The Bidder should have an average annual financial turnover of at least INR 15,00,000 over the last three (3) financial years (supported by audited statements / CA certificate).
  7. The Bidder shall not be blacklisted, debarred or banned by any Central / State Government department, public sector undertaking, or funding agency as on the date of submission.
  8. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of supplying to projects in Sikkim / North-East / hilly terrain and capability of door-delivery to remote sites.

Technical Proposal Documents

The Technical Proposal should include:

  • Organisation Profile & Dealership / Authorisation certificates for key brands.
  • Understanding of the Assignment and proposed delivery methodology (including logistics to West Sikkim).
  • Detailed Delivery Schedule (within 21 days).
  • Make / Model / Brand confirmation for every line item.
  • Relevant Experience (supply orders / invoices of similar materials).
  • GST, PAN, Trade Licence, MSME Certificate (if applicable).
  • Cancelled cheque / bank details.

7. Financial Bid Format

Bidders shall quote rates for the complete supply on the basis of the Bill of Materials above. The summary format below shall be used for the Financial Bid. Unit rates shall be inclusive of all taxes, transportation, loading/unloading and delivery at site. GST shall be shown separately if applicable.

S.NoParticularBrand OfferedUnitUnit Price (INR)Total (INR)
1GCI Sheet 45 mm 20’×4′60 Nos.
2Iron Steel Bar 4 inch40 Nos.
3Iron Steel Bar 2 inch50 Nos.
4Iron Steel Bar 1.5 inch60 Nos.
5Bricks 1st Quality7000 Nos.
6Nails400 Nos.
7Iron Cutter Blade10 Nos.
8Mangara100 ft/Nos.
9Branding & Signage (Radium) – 3 sides3 sides
10Water Purifier (Hot & Cold)1 No.
11Umbrella Bank (Customised)20 Nos.
12Wi-Fi with 6-month subscription1 Set
13Off-Grid Solar System (2 kW complete: 4×500W Panel + 3kW Inverter + 2×200Ah Battery + installation)1 Set
14Transportation, loading, unloading & site delivery (all inclusive)—Lumpsum
TOTAL (Inclusive of all taxes & delivery)

8. Evaluation

Proposals will be evaluated on the basis of:

  • Technical compliance – brand confirmation, authorisation, quality of materials offered.
  • Relevant experience in supply of similar materials and capability of delivery to West Sikkim.
  • Completeness of documentation and responsiveness.
  • Financial proposal (value for money, reasonableness of rates, total within ceiling).
  • Preference for local / North-East based suppliers and authorised dealers of preferred brands.

Only technically qualified bidders’ financial bids will be opened. PPHF reserves the right to seek clarifications, negotiate rates or reject any or all bids.

9. Payment Terms

Payment shall be made in three (3) instalments as follows:

  • Part 1 – Advance Payment (30%): Thirty percent (30%) of the total contract value shall be released as advance against submission of a proforma invoice / request letter and a bank guarantee or equivalent security (if required by PPHF) within seven (7) days of issuance of the Work Order / Purchase Order.
  • Part 2 – On Delivery & Inspection (50%): Fifty percent (50%) of the total contract value shall be released upon successful delivery of all materials at the project site, verification and acceptance by PPHF / authorised representative / Panchayat President, and submission of delivery challan, tax invoice and inspection report.
  • Part 3 – Final Payment on Installation & Handover (20%): The remaining twenty percent (20%) of the total contract value shall be released after successful installation and commissioning of the solar system, water purifier, branding/signage and Wi-Fi (as applicable), final handover to the Panchayat President, and submission of completion certificate / handover note duly signed by the authorised representatives.

All payments shall be made through bank transfer / NEFT / RTGS against valid tax invoices. No interest shall be payable on delayed payments arising from incomplete documentation or non-compliance by the supplier.

10. General Terms and Conditions of Contract

ClauseProvision
Validity of OfferBids shall remain valid for sixty (60) days from the last date of submission.
Quoted RatesRates shall be firm, fixed and inclusive of all materials, transport, loading/unloading, delivery at site and applicable taxes (GST shown separately if required). No price escalation will be allowed.
Delivery PeriodComplete supply and delivery (including installation support) within 21 days from the date of Work Order / Purchase Order.
Quality & InspectionAll materials are subject to inspection and verification by PPHF or its authorised representative / ADC (Dev.) / Panchayat. Sub-standard or non-conforming materials shall be replaced at the Bidder’s cost.
Liquidated DamagesFor delay beyond the delivery period, LD of 0.5% of the order value per week (subject to a ceiling of 10%) shall be levied.
WarrantyManufacturer’s warranty on solar panels, inverter, batteries, water purifier and other equipment shall be passed on to the beneficiary. Minimum 1-year warranty on workmanship for installed items.
Sub-contractingSub-contracting or assignment without PPHF’s prior written consent is prohibited.
TerminationPPHF may terminate the order for breach, non-delivery, insolvency or unsatisfactory performance, after due notice.
Force MajeureNeither party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond reasonable control, duly notified in writing within 7 days.
Dispute ResolutionDisputes shall first be settled amicably; failing which, by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, language English.
JurisdictionSubject to arbitration, the courts at Delhi shall have exclusive jurisdiction; the contract is governed by the laws of India.

11. Submission Details

Interested suppliers / dealers shall submit:

  • Agency / Firm Profile and Dealership / Authorisation certificates.
  • Technical Proposal (brand confirmation, delivery plan, experience).
  • Financial Proposal (filled BOQ format above) – password-protected if submitted by email.
  • GST Registration Certificate, PAN Card, Trade Licence.
  • MSME Certificate (if applicable).
  • Cancelled cheque / bank details.
  • Any other supporting documents as per eligibility criteria.

Email: procurement@pphfglobal.org
Last Date for Submission: 5th October 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Subject Line: Cafeteria Materials Hillary Park – PPHF/5031/26-27

You are requested to provide your confidential sealed hard copy or soft copy through email (Financial Bid password-protected) at the above address / email by 17:30 hours on 5th October 2026. Quotations submitted on time will be opened at 15:00 Hrs. on 6th October 2026. Late quotes will be rejected.

E-mail Submission Protocol

  • The Technical Bid shall be sent as a single PDF.
  • The Financial / Price Bid shall be sent as a SEPARATE password-protected (encrypted) PDF. The price file MUST NOT be readable without a password.
  • The password to the Financial Bid shall NOT be sent with the bid. It shall be furnished by the Bidder only when called for by PPHF.
  • Any price information disclosed in the unprotected Technical Bid or the e-mail body shall render the bid liable to rejection.

12. Disclaimer

PPHF reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals without assigning any reason. PPHF may cancel or modify the procurement process at any stage without incurring any liability.

title: Request for Proposal (RFP) Ref. No.: PPHF/5031/26-27/Indoor Stadium Yuksom
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) Renovation of Gym Hall and Construction of Indoor Stadium at Yuksom, Sikkim Ref. No.: PPHF/5031/26-27/Indoor Stadium Yuksom Date…
html:
Request for Proposal (RFP)
Renovation of Gym Hall and Construction of Indoor Stadium at Yuksom, Sikkim
Ref. No.: PPHF/5031/26-27/Indoor Stadium Yuksom
Date: 29th September 2026

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF), New Delhi, invites sealed/digital quotations under a Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) for the Renovation of Gym Hall and Construction of Indoor Stadium at Yuksom, Sikkim (Financial Year 2026–2027) as per the specifications and requirements detailed below.

RFP Details

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5031/26-27/Indoor Stadium Yuksom
Date of Issue of RFP29th September 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission5th October 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs6th October 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected)

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Civil Contractors, Construction Agencies, Registered Builders and Fabrication Agencies for the renovation of existing Gym Hall and construction of a pre-fabricated Indoor Stadium at Yuksom, Sikkim under the PPHF – Rural Infrastructure Transformation Programme.

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-supported project for strengthening community sports and fitness infrastructure through essential civil renovation of the existing RCC Gym Hall (approx. 75 ft × 30 ft) and construction of a new pre-fabricated MS structure Indoor Stadium (approx. 27 ft × 22 ft) complete with table tennis / multi-purpose court, flooring, roofing, toilets and related works as per approved specifications and Bill of Quantities.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Yuksom and surrounding rural communities in Sikkim have limited access to safe, functional indoor sports and fitness facilities. The existing Gym Hall requires structural renovation, floor protection, painting, toilet upgradation and provision for multi-activity use (table tennis, carrom, kids’ badminton). A new compact indoor stadium is required to house a dedicated table-tennis / multi-purpose court under a pre-fabricated MS post & purlin structure with GI / colour-coated roofing.

Upgrading these facilities will improve community health, youth engagement, physical fitness opportunities and social cohesion, while creating a safe, weather-protected space for year-round indoor sports activities.

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to renovate the existing Gym Hall and construct a new pre-fabricated Indoor Stadium at Yuksom so that the community has access to a functional, hygienic and multi-purpose indoor sports & fitness facility. The intervention will deliver a renovated RCC gym space with modern flooring, upgraded toilets and a new weather-protected court for table tennis and related activities.

2.3 Objectives

  • To renovate and upgrade the existing Gym Hall (RCC structure ≈ 75 ft × 30 ft).
  • To construct a new pre-fabricated MS Indoor Stadium (≈ 27 ft × 22 ft) with GI / colour-coated sheet roofing.
  • To provide interlocking gym floor mats, table-tennis court flooring and related sports surfaces.
  • To upgrade toilets, drainage, doors, windows, railing and painting works.
  • To create a safe, clean and functional environment for community sports, fitness and youth activities.
  • To complete all works to CPWD / DSR / IS standards within the stipulated timeline.

2.4 Targeted Beneficiaries

Direct Beneficiaries:

  • Youth, students and community members using gym and indoor sports facilities.
  • Local sports clubs, schools and village institutions.
  • Women and children seeking safe indoor activity spaces.

Indirect Beneficiaries:

  • Wider community of Yuksom and surrounding villages.
  • Local administration and Block Development structures through improved public infrastructure.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of civil renovation of the Gym Hall and construction of the pre-fabricated Indoor Stadium (including table-tennis court) at the BAC Area / Yuksom site. All works shall conform to relevant CPWD / DSR specifications, IS codes and local building bye-laws.

Key project dimensions (approximate):

  • Gym Hall (renovation – existing RCC structure): 75 ft × 30 ft
  • Indoor Stadium / Table Tennis Court (new pre-fabricated MS structure): 27 ft × 22 ft
  • Total approximate area under intervention: ≈ 6,094 sq.ft

A. Site Preparation, Earthwork & Foundation

  • Site clearance, layout and land levelling.
  • Excavation in soil in hilly area (mechanical means) including cutting, trimming of side slopes and disposal of excavated earth (leads as required).
  • Hand-packed stone soling in building works with clean hard selected stones.
  • Providing & laying cement concrete 1:2:4 / 1:3:6 / 1:4:8 as per design (PCC for plinth, foundations and flooring base).
  • Stone plum wall / CRSM / foundation masonry as required.
  • Backfilling with approved material and compaction.

B. Structural & Superstructure Works (Gym Hall Renovation)

  • Dismantling of selected walls / chipping of old roof surface as required for renovation.
  • Half-brick / full-brick work in cement mortar 1:4 for partition / repairs.
  • 12 mm / 15 mm cement plaster (1:3 or 1:4) on internal and external surfaces.
  • Plaster of Paris putty 2 mm thick over plastered surfaces.
  • Cement plaster skirting (18 mm thick, 30 cm height) where specified.
  • Repair / replacement of RCC elements if identified during inspection.

C. Pre-Fabricated Indoor Stadium Structure (New Construction)

  • Supplying, fabricating, fitting and fixing steel tubular trusses / MS posts & purlins including cutting, hoisting, fixing in position and applying priming coat of approved steel primer (welded and bolted).
  • 24 BWG GP / GCI / colour-coated galvanized sheet roofing (JSW / Jindal / Tata or equivalent) with corrugation, G.I. hooks, bolts, nuts, bitumen and limpet washers.
  • Ridges / hips of 60 cm overall width of plain 24 BWG galvanized sheet.
  • Pre-painted eaves board with dressed timber beading and M.S. rod brackets.
  • MS pipe new structure, railing and related steel works.
  • ACP board branding and steel pipe board branding as directed.

D. Doors, Windows, Frames & Joinery

  • Providing / fitting / fixing of dressed sal timber (or approved timber) in frames for doors.
  • Waterproof flush door shutters (ISI certified) – solid block hard core with decorative faces.
  • Brass bright finished butt hinges, sliding door bolts, tower bolts and handles (chromium plated / copper oxidized as specified).
  • MS windows and frames (new) and aluminium works for partitions / windows / ventilators (anodized, IS 733 / IS 1285).

E. Flooring, Sports Surfaces & Finishes

  • Providing and fixing gym floor mat of 24 mm interlocking tiles for heavy workouts (approx. mat size 64 cm × 64 cm) covering gym area and related spaces.
  • Table tennis court flooring / surface as per approved specification.
  • Vitrified / ceramic glazed floor tiles (Kajaria / Simpolo or equivalent) in washrooms, office and selected areas laid on cement mortar bed with pointing.
  • White or coloured glazed tiles in washroom walls / dados.

F. Painting & Protective Coatings

  • Providing and painting with acrylic exterior paints (Excel / Weather Shield or equivalent) – two or more coats with primer.
  • Deluxe multi-surface interior paint / plastic emulsion (Asian Paints / Berger or equivalent) – two or more coats.
  • Snowcem / Durocem washing (three coats) where specified.
  • French spirit polishing on timber doors (two or more coats).
  • Priming and painting of all MS / steel surfaces.

G. Toilet Upgradation, Plumbing & Drainage

  • Upgradation of toilets (minimum 2 units) including dismantling old plaster/skirting, new plaster, POP, paint, ceramic floor & wall tiles.
  • Sanitary fixtures – WC pans (Indian / European), wash basins, cisterns, urinals as required.
  • CPVC / SCI pipes, bib cocks, stop cocks, gratings and related plumbing.
  • Drainage works and site protective works.
  • High-density polyethylene water storage tank (Sintex or equivalent, 500 litres) with man-hole lid and locking arrangement.

H. Ancillary & Finishing Items

  • Provision for table tennis, carrom board and kids’ badminton court (space & surface readiness).
  • Sign board.
  • Haulage, loading & unloading of materials (cement, steel, sand, aggregates, stone) as per actual leads.
  • All incidental works necessary for complete and functional handover.

I. Deliverables

  • Inception Report & Work Plan (including bar chart / Gantt).
  • Technical inspection report and final repair / construction plan with photographs.
  • Site clearance, excavation and foundation completion report.
  • Structural / steel fabrication and roofing completion report.
  • Flooring, painting, toilet and plumbing completion report.
  • Final Project Completion Report with Measurement Book (MB) abstract, photographs, as-built drawings and financial statement.
  • Warranty / Defect Liability documentation.

4. Timeline

The entire assignment shall be completed within 5 (five) months from the date of the Work Order or handing over of the site, whichever is later. A detailed month-wise implementation schedule / bar chart shall be submitted with the Technical Proposal.

5. Applicable Indian Compliance & Statutory Acts

Bidders must ensure all construction, materials, labour deployment, documentation and process workflows strictly comply with the following statutory requirements:

  • CPWD Specifications / Delhi Schedule of Rates (DSR) relevant items and IS Codes for materials and workmanship.
  • National Building Code (NBC) of India – relevant provisions.
  • The Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 and Rules.
  • Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and applicable State labour laws (Sikkim).
  • GST & Tax Regulations: CGST and SGST compliance with valid GSTIN.
  • MSMED Act, 2006: Benefits applicable to registered MSMEs.
  • Relevant BIS / ISI standards for steel, sheets, tiles, paints and sanitary fittings.
  • Environmental norms for disposal of construction waste.

6. Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for evaluation, a Bidder must satisfy all the following minimum eligibility conditions and furnish documentary proof in the Technical Bid:

  1. The Bidder shall be a legally constituted entity (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company, registered society or registered contractor) operating in India.
  2. The Bidder shall hold a valid Trade Licence / Contractor Registration and a valid GST Registration Certificate.
  3. The Bidder shall hold a valid PAN issued by the Income-tax Department.
  4. The Bidder should have satisfactorily executed similar civil construction / building renovation / pre-fabricated steel structure / sports facility projects during the last three (03) financial years (supported by work orders and completion certificates).
  5. The Bidder should have an average annual financial turnover of at least INR 30,00,000 – 50,00,000 over the last three (3) financial years (supported by audited statements / CA certificate).
  6. The Bidder shall not be blacklisted, debarred or banned by any Central / State Government department, public sector undertaking, or funding agency as on the date of submission.
  7. The Bidder shall submit relevant work orders / purchase orders and completion certificates as evidence of successful execution of similar assignments.
  8. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of working in hilly / North-East terrain or on community sports / gymnasium facilities.
  9. The Bidder shall have qualified civil engineers / site supervisors and capability to execute steel fabrication and roofing works of specified quality.

Technical Proposal

The Technical Proposal should include the following:

  • Organisation Profile
  • Understanding of the Assignment
  • Proposed Methodology and Approach (including quality control, safety and hill-area construction considerations)
  • Detailed Work Plan & Five-Month Implementation Schedule (Bar Chart)
  • Team Composition, CVs of Key Personnel (Civil Engineer / Site Supervisor / Fabrication In-charge) and Roles
  • Quality Assurance & Quality Control Plan
  • Safety, Health & Environment (SHE) Plan
  • Risk Identification and Mitigation Plan (especially for hilly site, monsoon and material logistics)
  • Relevant Experience in Similar Assignments (civil renovation / pre-fab steel structures / sports facilities)
  • Details of Previous/Current Clients and Client References
  • Any Proposed Value-Adds or Innovations

Due Diligence and Documents to be Submitted

PPHF will conduct due diligence on each Bidder before award. The Technical Bid must contain self-attested copies of the following documents. Failure to submit any mandatory document may render the bid liable to rejection.

DocumentParticulars / Evidence Required
Constitution / registrationCertificate of incorporation, partnership deed, registration certificate or proprietorship proof; Contractor Registration (CPWD / PWD preferred).
Trade LicenceValid trade / business licence / contractor licence.
GST RegistrationGST Registration Certificate (GSTIN) and a recent GST return acknowledgement.
PAN CardCopy of PAN of the firm / proprietor.
ExperienceWork orders and Completion Certificates for similar civil / renovation / steel structure works in the last 3 years.
Financial standingAudited financial statements / CA-certified turnover for the last 3 years; cancelled cheque / bank details.
Team CredentialsCVs of key personnel (Civil Engineer / Site Supervisor / Fabrication In-charge) proposed for the assignment.
Statutory registrationsEPF & ESI registration (where applicable); labour licence (where applicable).

Bidding Mechanism:

  • Cover 1 (Technical Bid): Contains Signed RFP Copy, Methodology, Team CVs, GST/PAN Registration, MSME Certificate (if applicable), Work Orders & Completion Certificates, and Client List.
  • Cover 2 (Financial Bid): Itemized BOQ in INR including base cost, applicable GST, and all incidental charges.

7. Financial Bid Format (BOQ Template)

Bidders shall quote rates for the complete work on the basis of the detailed Bill of Quantities (BOQ) derived from the Detailed Estimate and EOI scope. The summary format below shall be used for the Financial Bid. Detailed item-wise rates matching the BOQ quantities shall be annexed.

S. No.Item / Service ParticularsUnit Price (INR)GST (%)Total incl. GST
1Site clearance, layout, earthwork excavation & land levelling
2Stone soling, PCC, foundation masonry, CRSM, backfilling
3RCC works, brick work, plaster, POP putty & skirting (Gym Hall)
4Steel tubular trusses / MS posts & purlins, fabrication & erection
524 BWG GP / GCI / colour-coated sheet roofing, ridges, eaves board
6Doors, windows, frames, aluminium partitions, hardware
7Gym interlocking floor mats (24 mm) & table tennis court surface
8Vitrified / ceramic tiles (floor & wall) – washrooms, office & selected areas
9Painting – acrylic exterior, multi-surface interior, steel primer & finish
10Toilet upgradation, sanitary fixtures, plumbing & drainage
11Railing, MS pipe structure, ACP / steel branding, water tank, sign board
12Haulage, loading/unloading, contingencies, site development & transport
TOTAL

Also Included on Financial Proposal

The Financial Proposal should provide a detailed and itemized cost breakdown matching the detailed BOQ quantities for the following major components:

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)

Intervention towards Quality Education and Recovery of Drop-outs

Renovation of Primary Schools at Thingling & Tsozo

Yuksam Block, Sikkim | Financial Year 2026–2027

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5031/26-27/Primary Schools Yuksam
Date of Issue of RFP30th September 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission5th October 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs6th October 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected)

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Civil Contractors, Construction Agencies, Registered Builders and Fabrication Agencies for the renovation of Primary Schools at Thingling and Tsozo, Khecheperi under Yuksam Block, Sikkim under the PPHF – Intervention towards Quality Education and Recovery of Drop-outs Programme.

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-supported project for strengthening primary education infrastructure through essential civil renovation of existing Primary School buildings at Thingling and Tsozo. The works include RCC repair, brick masonry, flooring repair and maintenance, plaster, railing, doors and windows, ACP/Steel board branding, paints, drainage and related items as per approved specifications and Bill of Quantities.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Yuksam Block and surrounding rural communities in Sikkim face challenges of inadequate school infrastructure contributing to learning gaps and drop-outs at the primary level. The existing Primary School buildings at Thingling and Tsozo require structural repair, flooring, plaster, doors/windows, painting, drainage and branding works to create a safe, functional and conducive learning environment.

Upgrading these facilities will support quality education, improve student retention, enhance learning outcomes and contribute to recovery of drop-outs, while creating a safe and weather-protected space for primary education activities.

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to renovate the existing Primary School buildings at Thingling and Tsozo, Yuksam Block so that students have access to a functional, hygienic and safe learning facility. The intervention will deliver renovated school spaces with improved structural integrity, modern flooring, upgraded doors/windows, painting, drainage and branding as per the Detailed Estimates and the Expression of Interest (EOI) scope.

2.3 Objectives

  • To renovate and upgrade the Primary School buildings at Thingling and Tsozo under Yuksam Block.
  • To execute RCC repair works, brick masonry, flooring repair & maintenance, plaster, railing, doors & windows.
  • To provide ACP Board Branding, Steel Pipe Board Branding, paints and drainage works.
  • To create a safe, clean and functional environment for quality primary education and recovery of drop-outs.
  • To complete all works to CPWD / DSR / IS standards within the stipulated timeline.

2.4 Targeted Beneficiaries

Direct Beneficiaries:

  • Primary school students of Thingling and Tsozo Primary Schools.
  • Teachers and school staff.
  • Parents and local community members supporting education.

Indirect Beneficiaries:

  • Wider community of Yuksam Block and surrounding villages.
  • Local administration and Block Development structures through improved public education infrastructure.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of civil renovation of Primary Schools at Thingling and Tsozo under Yuksam Block. All works shall conform to relevant CPWD / DSR specifications, IS codes and local building bye-laws.

Key project sites:

  • Primary School at Thingling under Yuksam Block
  • Primary School at Tsozo, Khecheperi under Yuksam Block

A. Site Preparation & Preparatory Works

  • Chipping of old structure and preparatory works as per Detailed Estimate.
  • Site clearance and preparation for renovation works.

B. RCC Works & Structural Repairs

  • Providing & Laying in position 1:1.5:3 mix reinforced cement concrete (RCC) of nominal mix excluding cost of form work, finishing & reinforcements with Recron 3S fibre as directed.
  • Providing, fixing and removing form work for casting R.C.C items (square columns) with imported timber.
  • Supplying, bending and placing in position of Tor steel reinforcement in all R.C.C works including cost of binding wires.
  • P/L c.c 1:3:6 mix, CRSM 1:3:6 mix, 1:1.5:3 mix R.C.C, 1:2:4 mix P.C.C as per EOI scope.

C. Brick Masonry & Plaster Works

  • Providing and laying first class brick work in half brick thick in superstructure with 1:4 cement mortar including carriage of bricks, curing etc.
  • Providing and Laying 12 mm thick cement plaster (1:3 mix) in single coat including finishing even and smooth and curing.
  • Providing and laying plaster of paris putty of 2 mm thick over plastered surface (Asian Paints / Berger Paints or equivalent).
  • Providing and Laying of 18 mm thick 30 cm height cement plaster skirting with cement mortar 1:3 finished with floating coat of neat cement.

D. Doors, Windows, Frames & Hardware

  • Providing / fitting / fixing of dressed sal timber (locally available) in all types of frames for doors.
  • Providing, fitting and fixing water proof flush door shutters (ISI certified) – solid block hard core construction with 3 mm teak ply decorative type, including hinges.
  • Providing & fixing brass bright finished butt hinges, sliding door bolts, tower bolts and handles (chromium plated / copper oxidized as specified).
  • Providing and fixing anodized aluminium works for doors, windows, ventilators and partitions (IS 733 and IS 1285).

E. Roofing, Trusses & Steel Works

  • Supplying, fabricating, fitting and fixing steel tubular trusses including cutting, hoisting, fixing and applying priming coat of approved steel primer.
  • P/F/F of 24 BWG GCI sheet roofing with lapping of 150 mm with G.I. hooks, bolts, nuts, bitumen and limpet washers.
  • P/F/F ridges or hips of 60 cm overall width of plain 24 BWG Galvanized Sheet.
  • Providing, fitting and fixing 23 cm deep 24 BWG Pre-painted HULAS sheet eaves board with dressed sal timber beading and M.S. Rod brackets.
  • Railing works as specified.

F. Flooring & Finishes

  • Flooring repair and maintenance works.
  • Providing and Laying white or coloured glazed vitrified tiles of classic colour or equivalent in flooring / dados laid on bed of 15 mm cm 1:3 with flush pointing.

G. Painting & Protective Coatings

  • Providing and painting with acrylic exterior paints (Excel / Weather Shield or equivalent) – two or more coats.
  • Providing and painting with plastic emulsion paint of two or more coats on new surface (Asian Paints / Berger Paints).
  • Providing washing of three coats of Snowcem / Durocem.
  • Providing and French spirit polishing two or more coats on doors.
  • Priming and painting of all MS / steel surfaces.

H. Branding, Drainage & Ancillary Items

  • ACP Board Branding and Steel Pipe Board Branding as directed.
  • Drainage repair & maintenance works.
  • Providing and placing high density polyethylene water storage tank (Sintex or equivalent, 500 litres) with man-hole lid and locking arrangement.
  • Sign board.
  • Haulage, loading & unloading of materials (cement, steel, sand, aggregates, stone) as per actual leads.
  • All incidental works necessary for complete and functional handover.

To be considered for evaluation, a Bidder must satisfy all the following minimum eligibility conditions and furnish documentary proof in the Technical Bid:

  8. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of working in hilly / North-East terrain or on school / education facility projects.
  9. The Bidder shall have qualified civil engineers / site supervisors and capability to execute the specified quality of works.

html:
PPHF/5031/26-27/Social Events

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)

Strengthening Primary Health Centres (PHCs) with Repair, Renovation and Medical Equipment Support

Financial Year 2026–2027

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5049/26-27/PHC Strengthening
Date of Issue of RFP15th August 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission21st August 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs24th August 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected)

Note: This RFP carries reference no. PPHF/5049/26-27, the same number used on the "Construction of High-Raised Community Sanitation Station" RFP issued the same day. If these are meant to be two distinct tenders, consider giving each a unique reference number before publishing.

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Civil Contractors, Construction Agencies, Registered Builders, Medical Equipment Suppliers and Service Providers for the repair, renovation and medical equipment support of selected Primary Health Centres (PHCs) under the PPHF – Rural Infrastructure Transformation Programme (HRDP).

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-supported project (supported by HDFC Bank Parivartan) for strengthening Primary Health Centres through essential civil repairs, sanitation improvement and provision of critical medical examination & diagnostic equipment. The selected agency will undertake complete civil renovation works including surface preparation, plastering, painting, flooring, toilet renovation, plumbing, and supply & installation of specified medical equipment as per approved specifications and Bill of Quantities.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Primary Health Centres serve as the first point of contact for rural communities seeking healthcare services. However, many PHCs operate with deteriorated infrastructure, inadequate sanitation facilities, outdated examination areas, and insufficient medical equipment, affecting the quality and accessibility of healthcare.

Poor physical conditions discourage patients from utilizing public healthcare facilities, while the lack of essential diagnostic equipment limits the ability of healthcare providers to deliver timely diagnosis and treatment.

Strengthening PHCs through targeted infrastructure repairs and equipment support will improve the safety and functionality of healthcare facilities, enhance patient comfort and service quality, strengthen diagnostic and primary treatment capacity, improve hygiene and infection prevention, increase public confidence in government healthcare services, and support equitable healthcare access in rural communities.

This intervention aligns with national health priorities and contributes to SDG 3 (Good Health & Well-being), SDG 6 (Clean Water & Sanitation), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to strengthen selected Primary Health Centres by undertaking essential civil repairs, improving sanitation facilities (including toilet renovation), and equipping the centres with critical medical equipment required for quality primary healthcare delivery. The intervention will create safe, functional, hygienic and patient-friendly healthcare facilities capable of delivering efficient outpatient and primary healthcare services while improving the working environment for healthcare providers.

2.3 Objectives

  • To repair and upgrade essential infrastructure in selected Primary Health Centres.
  • To improve sanitation, accessibility and patient convenience within PHCs.
  • To provide essential medical examination and diagnostic equipment.
  • To strengthen the quality and efficiency of primary healthcare services.
  • To improve patient satisfaction and utilization of public health facilities.
  • To create a safe, clean and functional environment for both healthcare providers and patients.

2.4 Targeted Beneficiaries

Direct Beneficiaries:

  • Rural patients accessing PHC services.
  • Pregnant women and mothers.
  • Children requiring routine healthcare services.
  • Elderly patients.
  • Healthcare workers including doctors, nurses and paramedical staff.

Indirect Beneficiaries:

  • Communities residing within the PHC catchment areas.
  • Village Health & Sanitation Committees.
  • Local health administration through strengthened healthcare infrastructure.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of civil repair & renovation works and supply & installation of medical equipment at the selected PHC(s). All works shall conform to relevant CPWD / DSR specifications, IS codes and local building bye-laws.

A. Civil Works – Surface Preparation, Plastering & Finishing

  • Removing white or colour wash by scraping and sand papering and preparing the surface smooth including necessary repairs to scratches etc. complete (Exterior walls).
  • Dismantling old plaster or skirting, taking out joints and cleaning the surface for plaster including disposal of rubbish to the dumping ground within 50 metres lead (Interior & Exterior).
  • 12 mm cement plaster of mix 1:4 (1 cement : 4 fine sand) on interior walls.
  • 15 mm cement plaster on the rough side of single or half brick wall of mix 1:4 (1 cement : 4 fine sand) on exterior walls.

  • Finishing walls with Acrylic Smooth exterior paint of required shade – New work (Two or more coats applied @ 1.67 ltr/10 sqm over and including priming coat of exterior primer applied @ 2.20 kg/10 sqm).

B. Flooring Works – Vitrified Floor Tiles

PPHF/5031/26-27/Social Events

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)

Construction of High-Raised Community Sanitation Station

Gelapukhuri (Tinsukia, Assam) & Upokpi Khunou (Bishnupur, Manipur)

Financial Year 2026–2027

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5049/26-27/Community Sanitation Station
Date of Issue of RFP15th August 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission21st August 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs24th August 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected)

Note: This RFP carries reference no. PPHF/5049/26-27, the same number used on the "Strengthening Primary Health Centres (PHCs)" RFP issued the same day. If these are meant to be two distinct tenders, consider giving each a unique reference number before publishing.

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Civil Contractors, Construction Agencies, Registered Builders, and Service Providers for the construction of High-Raised Community Sanitation Station(s) at flood-prone locations in Gelapukhuri, Tinsukia (Assam) and Upokpi Khunou, Bishnupur (Manipur).

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-supported project for establishment of climate-resilient, gender-segregated community sanitation facilities. The selected agency will undertake complete civil construction including foundation, superstructure, plumbing, sanitary fittings, electrical works, roofing, finishing, septic tank, soak pit, water supply system and related infrastructure as per approved drawings and specifications.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Flooding is a major challenge affecting rural communities in Assam and Manipur. Seasonal floods frequently damage sanitation infrastructure, contaminate groundwater, and force people to practice open defecation, increasing the risk of waterborne and communicable diseases. Many households lack Individual Household Latrines (IHHLs) due to space constraints, financial limitations, and flood vulnerability.

Community sanitation facilities therefore become a critical solution to ensure safe sanitation access. A high-raised community sanitation station is essential to sustain sanitation services during floods, prevent overflow and environmental contamination, reduce health risks, enhance privacy, dignity and safety (especially for women, children and elderly), and support Open Defecation Free (ODF) goals.

This intervention aligns with national sanitation priorities and contributes to SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to establish fully functional, flood-resilient High-Raised Community Sanitation Station(s) comprising separate toilet and bathing cubicles for men and women, shared hand-washing facilities, cloth-washing platform, independent borewell-based water supply with overhead storage, solar lighting, septic tank / soak pit, and appropriate drainage systems.

2.3 Objectives

  • To establish flood-resilient, high-raised community sanitation station(s) in Gelapukhuri (Assam) and/or Upokpi Khunou (Manipur)
  • To reduce open defecation and improve environmental hygiene
  • To improve health, safety, privacy and dignity, particularly for women, children and elderly persons
  • To prevent groundwater contamination and disease outbreaks during floods
  • To promote community ownership and sustainable Operation & Maintenance (O&M) mechanisms
  • To generate 2–3 local employment opportunities for maintenance and cleaning

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end construction and commissioning of the High-Raised Community Sanitation Station as detailed below. All works shall conform to relevant CPWD / DSR specifications, IS codes and local building bye-laws.

A. Civil Works – Foundation, Plinth & Superstructure

  • Earthwork in excavation for foundation trenches (all kinds of soil) – as per BOQ quantities
  • Filling available excavated earth in trenches, plinth and sides of foundations
  • Supplying and filling in plinth with sand under floors
  • Plain Cement Concrete (PCC) 1:3:6 in footings and flooring
  • Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) 1:1.5:3 for footings, columns, pedestals, plinth beams, lintels and roof beams
  • Steel reinforcement (TMT bars Fe-500D or more) – including straightening, cutting, bending, placing and binding
  • Centering and shuttering for foundations, footings, columns, beams, lintels etc.
  • Brick work with common burnt clay FPS bricks (class designation 7.5) in CM 1:4 for foundation, plinth and superstructure
  • Half-brick masonry for partition walls in CM 1:3
  • High-raised plinth to ensure flood resilience

B. Roofing & Structural Steel

  • Structural steel work in single section for roofing support (approx. 800 kg)
  • Precoated galvanised iron profile sheets (0.50 mm TCT) for roofing
  • Precoated GI sheet roofing accessories – ridges plain (500–600 mm)

C. Doors, Windows, Ventilators & Aluminium Works

  • Powder-coated aluminium work for doors, windows and ventilators (approx. 90 kg)
  • Glazing with float glass panes of 4.0 mm thickness
  • Powder-coated aluminium covering sheets (2.5 mm)
  • Brass 100 mm mortice latch and lock for aluminium doors
  • Oxidised MS hinges 125 mm

D. Finishing Works

  • 15 mm cement plaster (1:4) on exterior walls
  • 12 mm cement plaster (1:4) on interior walls
  • Plaster of Paris putty (2 mm) over plastered surfaces
  • Acrylic Smooth exterior paint (two or more coats)
  • Interior wall painting with primer and two or more coats
  • Ceramic glazed floor tiles (300 × 300 mm) in WC and other areas
  • Ist quality ceramic glazed wall tiles for dados / skirting in WC areas

E. Sanitary & Plumbing Works

  • White vitreous china Orissa pattern WC pan with 100 mm SCI P/S trap, 10 L low-level PVC flushing cistern (6 nos.)
  • White vitreous china urinal basin with automatic flushing cistern (3 nos.)
  • White vitreous china wash basin with CI brackets, CP brass pillar taps and waste (2 nos.)
  • CP brass toilet paper holder (6 nos.)
  • Soil, waste and vent pipes – 100 mm dia sand cast iron S&S pipe
  • CPVC pipes of various diameters (15 mm, 20 mm, 25 mm, 40 mm)
  • Brass bib cock 15 mm (6 nos.)
  • CP brass shower rose 100 mm dia (6 nos.)
  • Brass stop cock 15 mm (5 nos.)
  • 100 mm sand cast iron floor traps / nahani traps (5 nos.)

F. Water Supply & Waste Management

  • Borewell / tubewell (100 mm dia casing) up to 6 m depth
  • Polyethylene water storage tank 5,000 litres (IS:12701) with cover and locking arrangement
  • Water pump (market rate)
  • Soak pit 2.5 m dia × 3.0 m deep with dry brick honey-comb shaft and SW drain pipe
  • Construction of Septic Tank complete (excavation, PCC, RCC slab, brickwork, plaster, reinforcement etc. as per BOQ)

G. Electrification Works

  • Wiring for light / exhaust fan points with 1.5 sq.mm FRLS PVC insulated copper conductor cable in PVC conduit (8 points)
  • Modular switches 5/6 A (10 nos.)
  • GI box with modular base & cover plate – 12 Module (2 nos.)
  • Solar-enabled lighting system (as per site requirement)

H. Facility Configuration (as per Concept Note)

  • Male Section: 2 toilet cubicles + 2 bathing cubicles
  • Female Section: 2 toilet cubicles + 2 bathing cubicles
  • Shared hand-wash area with basins
  • Cloth-washing platform with water taps
  • Perimeter fencing and controlled entry (if required)
  • Independent water supply and solar lighting

I. Deliverables

  • Inception Report & Work Plan (including bar chart / CPM)
  • Site Layout & Construction Drawings (if not already provided)
  • Foundation Completion Report with photographs
  • Plinth Level Completion Report
  • Superstructure & Roofing Completion Report
  • Plumbing, Sanitary & Electrical Completion Report
  • Finishing & Handing-over Report with as-built drawings
  • Final Project Completion Report with Measurement Book (MB) abstract, photographs and financial statement
  • Warranty / Defect Liability documentation

  • The Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 and Rules
  • Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and applicable State labour laws

The Bidder should have satisfactorily executed similar civil construction / building works / sanitation infrastructure projects during the last three (03) financial years (supported by work orders and completion certificates). Preference will be given to experience in North-Eastern region / flood-prone areas.
  5. The Bidder should have an average annual financial turnover of at least INR 40,00,000 – 50,00,000 over the last three (3) financial years (supported by audited statements / CA certificate).
  6. The Bidder shall not be blacklisted, debarred or banned by any Central / State Government department, public sector undertaking, or funding agency as on the date of submission.
  7. The Bidder shall submit relevant work orders / purchase orders and completion certificates as evidence of successful execution of similar assignments.
  8. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of working in hilly / North-Eastern terrain and/or construction of community toilets / sanitation complexes.
  9. The Bidder shall have qualified civil engineers / site supervisors and a dedicated construction team capable of deployment at the project site(s).

html:
PPHF/5031/26-27/Social Events

Request for Applications (RFA)

PROJECT RAKSHA

Rapid Formative Assessment (RFA)

Understanding Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) Awareness, Screening, Diagnostic Practices, and Care Pathways

Target LocationsKolhapur District (Maharashtra) & Tiruvallur District (Tamil Nadu)
Issuing OrganizationPeople to People Health Foundation (PPHF)
Project Duration1 Month (Including Final Report)
Application Deadline20th September 2026
Submission Emailprocurement@pphfglobal.org

1. Organization Background

PPHF is a health organization, working with a mission of transforming lives for improved health and wellbeing through locally driven solutions. We are registered as non-for-profit company under section 8 in India. (https://pphfglobal.org/)

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF) is a non-profit organization committed to strengthening public health in India through research, education, and policy advocacy. Its thematic portfolio includes maternal, child and adolescent health and nutrition; non-communicable diseases; infectious diseases; health-system strengthening; environmental and planetary health; and health innovation and technology.

2. Project Overview

PPHF is implementing a project to enhance the awareness, early screening and treatment of diabetes retinopathy (DR) among the diabetic population in Kolhapur District in Maharashtra and Tiruvallur District in Tamil Nadu.

For this purpose, PPHF is conducting a rapid formative qualitative assessment at the selected district level to understand the magnitude and nature of the diabetes retinopathy burden, existing screening and diagnostic practices, treatment pathways, and the availability and accessibility of care. The assessment will examine health-seeking behaviours and care pathways among people with diabetes, including when and where they seek care, how they navigate referral and treatment services and the treatment options available to them. It will also assess the availability, readiness and capacity of services across PHCs, CHCs, and district hospitals.

Therefore, the assessment will explore the barriers and enablers influencing screening, diagnosis, treatment initiation and continuity of care, including awareness and perceptions of diabetes retinopathy among patients and healthcare providers. The findings will help identify key gaps and opportunities for strengthening early identification, referral and access to appropriate and affordable diabetes retinopathy care at the district level.

In this regard, PPHF invites proposals from the eligible and competent agencies for Rapid formative Assessment (RFA).

3. Objectives of the Rapid Formative Research:

  • Understand the current landscape of DR including awareness, screening and detection practices, treatment-seeking patterns, and the types of care and treatment options currently available to people with diabetes.
  • Explore patient and community perspectives on DR careincluding knowledge, perceptions, beliefs, risk perceptions, health-seeking behaviour, treatment preferences and choices, and experiences of accessing and navigating available services.
  • Examine gaps in current policies, programmes and service delivery including supply-side and demand-side constraints that may contribute to missed opportunities for screening, delayed diagnosis, treatment drop-offs or inadequate follow-up.
  • Identify context-specific opportunities for action and generate evidence to guide the development of practical, scalable and sustainable interventions that can strengthen the DR care pathway and improve access to timely and appropriate care.

4. Key Activities & Methodology

  • Secondary Research & Desk Review: Conduct a desk review of national and state-level data, existing practices, guidelines, policies, and health systems literature to analyze current statistics on diabetes prevalence, Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) screening coverage, and recorded DR cases.
  • Stakeholder Mapping: Map key Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) and eye-health stakeholders across the state—including program managers, health facilities, non-profits, and specialist centers—with a specific focus on diabetes care and vision health.
  • Facility-Level Qualitative Assessment: Conduct In-Depth Interviews (IDIs) with key facility-level healthcare providers (e.g., medical officers, ophthalmologists, optometrists, and NCD staff) to evaluate facility readiness, service delivery, and current DR screening and management practices.
  • Community & Patient Perspectives: Execute Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) and IDIs with patients living with diabetes and DR to explore awareness, screening history, healthcare-seeking behavior, barriers to treatment adherence, and support needed to complete treatment.
  • Supply Chain & Diagnostic Infrastructure Assessment: Perform observational field visits to assess current supply chain practices, equipment availability (e.g., fundus cameras, diagnostic tools), and medication/treatment access for DR care at different tier facilities.
  • Health Information & Data Integration Analysis: Examine DR and diabetes data recording, tracking, and reporting mechanisms under the Health Management Information System (HMIS) and evaluate opportunities for integration with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and PM-JAY.
  • System Capacity & Service Utilization Evaluationn: Assess the capacity, efficiency, and referral pathways of the health system to deliver specialized DR services and evaluate overall patient utilization of screening and treatment facilities.
  • Gap Analysis & Strategic Opportunity Identification: Identify systemic, financial, logistical, and awareness gaps across the continuum of care, highlighting specific intervention points to improve early DR screening, patient navigation, treatment compliance, and holistic patient support.
  • Documentation & Actionable RecommendationsSynthesize findings into a comprehensive research report with concrete, data-backed recommendations detailing how stakeholders can bridge identified gaps and improve end-to-end support for DR patients

5. Time Frame & Deliverables

Methodology

The assessment will be carried out at two levels: communities and systems. Both secondary and primary data shall be utilized. The assessment will involve qualitative methods using In-depth Interviews (IDIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and stakeholder analysis, mapping and supply chain management on diabetes retinopathy.

A. Implementation Schedule (5-Week Timeline)

Time Frame and Plan: one month (including final report)

Activity Week 1 Week 2 Week 3 Week 4 Week 5
Conduct a desk review of relevant existing best practices, documents, guidelines, plans, policies, materials, and literature. Propose an implementation guide ✓
FFinalize tools for Data Collection and share with PPHF for alignment ✓
Data Collection: In-depth interviews and Focus Groups Discussions with Community and Health Facility Survey ✓ ✓
Document Findings and Suggestions of the RFA and submitting of final deliverables s ✓ ✓ ✓

B. Phased Deliverables

  • Weeks 1–2: Detailed study protocol (data collector training, field supervision plan, data collection tools), Literature Review, and Stakeholder Mapping.
  • Week 3: Draft Report with recommendations/findings under each activity, accompanied by a Summary PPT.
  • Weeks 4–5: Final Report (comprehensive detailed report + 2–4 page brief summary) and Final Presentation.

6. Eligibility Criteria

• The Agency should be a registered body (proprietary, partnership firm, company/society/trust) NGO and academic institute or a team of public health and health statistics experts.

  • • The Agency should be in existence for at least one-two years and have experience in research and evaluation.
  • • Previous work in similar sector is important.

7. Application Deadline:

Send your applications with a response to the said RFA, organization profile and work samples to procurement@pphfglobal.org .The last date of receiving applications is September 20, 2026.

Email Application To: procurement@pphfglobal.org
Application Deadline: 20th September 2026
Subject Line: Response to RFA - Project Raksha (Kolhapur & Tiruvallur)

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Farmers’ Producer Organisations (FPOs), Agri-Entrepreneurs, Seed Producers, Authorized Dealers, Organic Farming Agencies, and Service Providers for the establishment and operation of an Organic Seed Production Cluster for Lady Finger, Bottle Gourd, Spinach, Radish and Cauliflower.

PPHF intends to implement a CSR–Government convergence project for organic seed production, capacity building of farmers, and market linkage. The selected agency will undertake land preparation, organic cultivation, seed production, training, packaging, branding and buy-back of certified organic seed.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Access to quality organic seed remains a critical gap for small and marginal farmers practising organic agriculture. PPHF intends to establish an Organic Seed Production Cluster to produce high-quality organic seed of five key vegetable crops – Lady Finger (Okra), Bottle Gourd, Spinach, Radish and Cauliflower – while simultaneously building farmer capacity and creating a sustainable market linkage through buy-back arrangements.

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to establish a functional organic seed production cluster on 2 acres, Purchasing Organic Seed for Production 110 kg of organic seed(All five crops – 110 kg total, i.e. 22 kg per crop as the target) of the five target crops, train 20 farmers, supply organic inputs, undertake sorting, packaging and branding, and ensure buy-back cost of 1 kg of seed for further distribution/marketing.

2.3 Objectives

  • Establish a 2-acre organic seed production plot with proper land preparation and water infrastructure.
  • Supply Organic Seed for Production-110 kg of high-quality organic seed of Lady Finger, Bottle Gourd, Spinach, Radish and Cauliflower (All five crops – 110 kg total, i.e. 22 kg per crop as the target)
  • Supply and apply organic manure (vermicompost) and bio-pesticides / bio-insecticides / bio-fungicides.
  • Conduct exposure-cum-cultivation training for 20 farmers/persons at institution that help them to learn end to end process of this intervention
  • Undertake labour for sorting, grading and packaging of seed.
  • Provide marketing support through branded pouches (5,000 nos.) and install branding board at production plot
  • Facilitate buy-back of produced organic seed.
  • Submit complete production, training and financial reports.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end establishment and operation of the Organic Seed Production Cluster as detailed below:

A. Land Preparation & Infrastructure

  • Land preparation on 2 acres: Ploughing, chilling, sickling, forking and hand picking.
  • Installation of water connection from source – Sprinkler system and pipes suitable for hilly terrain covering 2 acres.
  • Erection of one Branding Board at the cluster site.

B. Organic Seed Production

  • Purchasing Organic Seed for Production: Lady Finger, Bottle Gourd, Spinach, Radish and Cauliflower targeting a total of 110 kg certified organic seed.( All five crops – 110 kg total, i.e. 22 kg per crop as the target.)
  • Application of Organic Manure – Vermicompost (10 MT).
  • Application of Biofit pesticides (40 Ltr), Biofit insecticides (40 Ltr) and Biofit fungicides (40 Ltr – note: quantity as per EOI).
  • Strict adherence to organic production protocols (no synthetic chemicals).

C. Capacity Building & Training

  • Conduct Exposure-cum-Cultivation Training for 20 persons covering organic seed production techniques, post-harvest handling and quality standards.
  • Submit Training Completion Report with attendance and photographs.

D. Post-Harvest, Packaging & Marketing Support

  • Labour for sorting, grading and packaging of seed (40 person-days).
  • Procurement and use of 5,000 branded pouches for seed packaging.
  • Facilitation of Buy-Back of organic seed at pre-agreed rates.

E. Deliverables

  • Inception Report & Work Plan
  • Land Preparation & Infrastructure Completion Report
  • Organic Input Application Log & Photographs
  • Seed Production Register (crop-wise quantity & quality)
  • Training Completion Report (with participant list & photos)
  • Packaging & Branding Report
  • Buy-Back Documentation & Proof of Payment/Receipt
  • Final Project Completion Report with Financial Statement

F. Indicative Component Quantities (from EOI)

4. Timeline

The entire assignment shall be completed within 5 months from the date of the Work Order or handing over of the land / site, whichever is later. A detailed month-wise implementation schedule shall be submitted with the Technical Proposal.

5. Applicable Indian Compliance & Statutory Acts

Bidders must ensure all cultivation, seed production, data handling, documentation and process workflows strictly comply with the following statutory requirements:

  • National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) / Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) guidelines issued by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / APEDA.
  • Seed Act, 1966 and Seed Rules, 1968 (as applicable to organic seed).
  • Data Protection & Privacy norms applicable to farmer-level personal data collection.
  • GST & Tax Regulations: Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) compliance with valid GSTIN.
  • MSMED Act, 2006: Benefits applicable to registered Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) per Govt. of India directives.
  • Labour & Safety Laws: Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and applicable provisions for personnel involved during field operations and training.

6. Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for evaluation, a Bidder must satisfy all the following minimum eligibility conditions and furnish documentary proof in the Technical Bid:

A. The Bidder shall be a legally constituted entity (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company, registered society, FPO, FPC or registered contractor) operating in India.

B. The Bidder shall hold a valid Trade Licence and a valid GST Registration Certificate.

C. The Bidder shall hold a valid PAN issued by the Income-tax Department.

D. The Bidder should have satisfactorily executed similar organic farming / seed production / farmer training / agri-input supply / market-linkage assignments during the last three (03) financial years (supported by work orders and completion certificates).

E. The Bidder should have an average annual financial turnover of at least INR 25,00,000 – 35,00,000 over the last three (3) financial years (supported by audited statements / CA certificate).

F. The Bidder shall not be blacklisted, debarred or banned by any Central / State Government department, public sector undertaking, or funding agency as on the date of submission.

G. The Bidder shall submit relevant work orders/purchase orders and completion certificates as evidence of successful execution of similar assignments.

H. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of working in hilly / North-Eastern terrain and/or providing end-to-end support including cultivation, training, packaging and buy-back.

I. The Bidder shall have qualified agronomists / seed technologists and a dedicated field team capable of deployment at the project site.

Technical Proposal

The Technical Proposal should include the following:

  1. Organisation Profile
  2. Understanding of the Assignment
  3. Proposed Methodology and Approach (including organic protocols, seed quality standards, data quality)
  4. Detailed Work Plan & Six-Month Implementation Schedule
  5. Team Composition, CVs of Key Personnel and Roles
  6. Organic Cultivation & Seed Production Protocol
  7. Training & Capacity Building Plan
  8. Post-Harvest, Packaging & Buy-Back Plan
  9. Risk Identification and Mitigation Plan
  10. Relevant Experience in Similar Assignments (organic farming / seed production / farmer training)
  11. Details of Previous/Current Clients and Client References
  12. Any Proposed Value-Adds or Innovations

Due Diligence and Documents to be Submitted

PPHF will conduct due diligence on each Bidder before award. The Technical Bid must contain self-attested copies of the following documents. Failure to submit any mandatory document may render the bid liable to rejection.

DocumentParticulars / Evidence Required

Bidding Mechanism:

  • Cover 1 (Technical Bid): Contains Signed RFP Copy, Methodology, Team CVs, GST/PAN Registration, MSME Certificate (if applicable), Work Orders & Completion Certificates, and Client List.
  • Cover 2 (Financial Bid): Itemized BOQ in INR including base cost, applicable GST, travel, accommodation, equipment and all incidental charges.

Also Included on Financial Proposal

The Financial Proposal should provide a detailed and itemized cost breakdown for the following components:

  11. Any Other Applicable Costs

E-mail Submission with Password Protection

In parallel with the hard copy, the Bidder shall e-mail the complete proposal to procurement@pphfglobal.org on or before the deadline, observing the following protocol:

  • The Technical Bid shall be sent as a single PDF.
  • The Financial / Price Bid shall be sent as a SEPARATE password-protected (encrypted) PDF. The price file MUST NOT be readable without a password.
  • The password to the Financial Bid shall NOT be sent with the bid. It shall be furnished by the Bidder only when called for by PPHF — i.e., at the time of financial-bid opening or on PPHF’s written / telephonic request to the qualified bidders.
  • The e-mail subject line shall read: PPHF/5032/26-27/Organic Seed Production Cluster.
  • Any price information disclosed in the unprotected Technical Bid or the e-mail body shall render the bid liable to rejection.

8. Evaluation

Proposals will be evaluated on the basis of:

  • Technical proposal quality, understanding of assignment, and methodology
  • Relevant experience in organic farming / seed production / farmer capacity building / agri-value chain
  • Proposed team composition and qualifications
  • Preference for firms / FPOs with prior experience in hilly / North-Eastern terrain
  • Financial proposal (value for money, completeness, and reasonableness of costs)

9. Payment Terms

Payment shall be linked with approved deliverables and shall be released against submission of invoices and acceptance of corresponding reports by PPHF, after statutory deductions (TDS / GST-TDS) and against valid tax invoices. Indicative milestone-based payment schedule:

  • 20% on approval of Inception Report and mobilisation
  • 30% on completion of Land Preparation, Water Infrastructure and first season sowing
  • 30% on submission of Seed Production Report, Training Completion and Packaging
  • 20% on Final Completion Report, Buy-Back documentation and acceptance

10. General Terms and Conditions of Contract

People to People Health Foundation

Request for Quotation (RFQ)
Assam Flood Response 2026

RFQ Reference: PPHF/RFQ/5061/01 Date of Issue: 14.08.2026

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF) invites sealed/email quotations from eligible NGOs, vendors, and firms for procurement, assembly, branding, distribution coordination, field implementation, and documentation of flood relief kits under the Assam Flood Response 2026 programme.

1. Background

PPHF, in partnership with Hero MotoCorp Limited (HMCL), is implementing a flood relief distribution programme for flood-affected communities across four districts of Assam: Golaghat, Jorhat, Charaideo, and Shivsagar. PPHF seeks to engage a qualified local implementation partner/vendor to undertake the comprehensive scope of work detailed below.

Indicative Distribution Volume: Approx. 2,350 kits across 4 districts

Golaghat550 Kits Jorhat600 Kits Charaideo600 Kits Shivsagar600 Kits

Indicative Timeline: Implementation from date of fund receipt through final report submission within 30 days. Subject to change based on road/flood conditions and field circumstances.

2. Scope of Work

  • Kit Procurement: Procurement of approved flood relief kit items as per specifications/quantities, supplier identification, quality assurance, and maintenance of records.
  • Assembly & Packaging: Consolidation, counting, checking, sealing, and quality checks of relief kits prior to dispatch.
  • Branding: Kit/packaging labels, stickers, banners, and backdrops at distribution locations per PPHF-approved guidelines.
  • Distribution Coordination: Alignment with designated Hero Dealers/dealer networks for distribution planning, beneficiary movement, and volunteer deployment.
  • Flag-Off Event: Coordination of formal flag-off event in Guwahati, subject to availability of the concerned MLA and dignitaries.
  • Schedule Sharing: Finalization and sharing of distribution schedules, beneficiary estimates, and logistics with PPHF and Hero Dealers.
  • Field Distribution: Deployment of field teams/volunteers for orderly, monitored distribution at approved locations.
  • Audio-Visual Documentation: Comprehensive photo and video documentation across all project stages.
  • Reporting: Submission of a comprehensive project completion report (location/date details, beneficiary counts, challenges, supporting invoices) within 30 days.
  • Record Keeping & Coordination: Maintenance of records and nomination of a field coordinator as a single point of contact.

3. Contents of Flood Relief Kit

Bucket Detergent Slippers Cotton maxi for women ORS Chlorine tablets Mosquito Net Mosquito Repellent sticks Sanitary Pads Bedsheet with pillow Mustard Oil Savlon Liquid LED Torch

4. Bid Submission Details

RFQ Opening Date: 14.08.2026
RFQ Closing Date: 18.08.2026, up to 5:00 PM IST
Mode of Submission: Email only
Submission Email: procurement@pphfglobal.org
Subject Line: "Quotation – Assam Flood Response 2026"

* Quotations received after the closing date/time or via other modes will not be considered.

5. Documents to be Submitted

  • Covering letter on organizational letterhead.
  • Item/service-wise price quotation (inclusive of applicable taxes, clearly indicated).
  • Company/organization profile and relevant work experience (preferably in flood relief/humanitarian logistics in Assam).
  • Copy of PAN Card.
  • GST Registration Certificate (if applicable).
  • MSME/Udyam Registration Certificate (if applicable).
  • Certificate of Incorporation/Registration (Trust Deed/Society Registration/Company Incorporation).
  • Cancelled cheque / bank account details.
  • Declaration of no conflict of interest.
  • References of similar past assignments, if any.

6. Evaluation Criteria

  • Technical capability and relevant field experience in Assam.
  • Financial competitiveness of the quoted price.
  • Compliance with statutory and documentation requirements.
  • Logistics and field presence in the specified districts.
  • Past track record in relief/humanitarian distribution programmes.

PPHF reserves the right to seek clarifications, negotiate terms, accept or reject any/all quotations without assigning reasons, and cancel this RFQ process at any stage.

7. Applicable Acts, Statutes & Compliance

The engagement, execution, and payments shall be governed by and subject to compliance with the following:

  • Indian Contract Act, 1872: Governing terms of engagement.
  • Income Tax Act, 2025: TDS deduction as per applicable rates; valid PAN required.
  • CGST Act, 2017 & Rules: Tax invoices under Rule 46/48; explicit GST indication required.
  • MSMED Act, 2006: Due consideration and payment timelines honored for registered MSMEs.
  • Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023: Beneficiary data and photos handled per privacy norms with consent.
  • Legal Status Statutes: Companies Act, 2013 / Societies Registration Act, 1860 / Indian Trusts Act, 1882.
  • Labour Laws & Local Regulations: Compliance for field staff/volunteers and Assam district administration/disaster management protocols.

8. General Terms

  • This RFQ does not constitute an offer or commitment by PPHF and does not entitle any bidder to compensation for proposal preparation costs.
  • The selected vendor must execute a formal Vendor Agreement/MoU with PPHF prior to commencement of work.
  • All branding and use of PPHF’s, HMCL’s, or partner logos require prior written approval.
  • Payment terms, advances (if any), and milestones will be finalized in the definitive agreement.

Contact for Queries:

Email: procurement@pphfglobal.org

Lajpat Nagar III, South Delhi
