REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)

Supply, Installation & Commissioning of 1 KW Rooftop Solar Power Systems under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana

Location: Sikkim

Financial Year 2026–2027

RFP Reference No.PPHF/5032/26-27/ Supply, Installation & Commissioning of 1 KW Rooftop Solar Power Systems under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
Date of Issue of RFP28 July 2026
Last Date & Time for Submission02 August 2026, up to 17:30 hrs
Date & Time of Opening of RFPs03 August 2026, at 15:00 hrs
Mode of SubmissionSealed Hard Copy and Email (Password-Protected)

1. Notice Inviting Tender / Quotation

Sealed/Digital Quotations are invited under Two-Bid System (Technical & Financial Bids) from eligible Manufacturers, Authorized Dealers, System Integrators, EPC Contractors, and Service Providers for the Supply, Installation & Commissioning of 1 KW Rooftop Solar Power Systems under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for 100 eligible households in Sikkim.

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-Government convergence project for installation of 1 KW rooftop solar systems. The selected agency will be responsible for complete supply of materials, installation, testing, commissioning, net-metering facilitation, and post-installation support for 100 beneficiary households identified through prior survey & technical assessment.

2. Background, Purpose & Objectives

2.1 Background

Access to affordable and clean electricity remains a challenge for deprived households. PPHF intends to implement a CSR-Government convergence project for installation of 1 KW rooftop solar systems under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for 100 eligible households in Sikkim.

2.2 Purpose

The assignment aims to supply, install, test, commission and hand over fully functional 1 KW on-grid rooftop solar power systems (net-metering enabled) at 100 eligible beneficiary households in Sikkim, ensuring compliance with MNRE / PM Surya Ghar guidelines and State Electricity Regulatory Commission norms.

2.3 Objectives

  • Supply of complete 1 KW rooftop solar systems as per approved technical specifications.
  • Installation and structural mounting of solar modules on beneficiary rooftops.
  • Electrical integration including DC/AC wiring, earthing, lightning protection, ACDB/DCDB.
  • Commissioning, testing and performance verification of each system.
  • Facilitation of net-metering approval and grid connectivity with the local DISCOM.
  • Training of beneficiaries on system operation, safety and basic maintenance.
  • Provision of 5-year comprehensive maintenance / replacement guarantee.
  • Submission of complete documentation, as-built drawings and handover certificates.

3. Scope of Work & Detailed Technical Specifications

The selected vendor/agency will be responsible for the end-to-end supply, installation, commissioning, documentation, net-metering support, and after-sales services as detailed below:

A. Supply of Materials

  • Procurement and supply of complete 1 KW on-grid rooftop solar power system components as per Annexure-I specifications.
  • All materials shall be new, unused, BIS/IEC certified, and of approved Tier-1 / specified makes.
  • Transportation, handling and safe storage of materials up to each beneficiary site in Sikkim.
  • Provision of all mounting hardware, cables, connectors, earthing materials and accessories.

B. Installation & Structural Works

  • Site readiness verification based on prior technical survey reports.
  • Fabrication and installation of Module Mounting Structure (pre-galvanized, 120-micron, wind load ≥150 kmph).
  • Mounting of Solar PV Modules (DCR Mono Half-cut / Bifacial, 540–600 W, 2 panels for ~1–1.2 kW).
  • Installation of Inverter / PCU (1 kVA Single MPPT On-Grid).
  • Laying of DC and AC cables with proper conduits, lugs and MC4 connectors.
  • Installation of ACDB, DCDB (with SPD), Chemical Earthing (3 pits) and Lightning Arrestor.
  • Ensuring structural integrity and aesthetic finish of all rooftop works.

C. Testing, Commissioning & Net-Metering

  • Pre-commissioning checks (insulation resistance, polarity, earthing continuity, etc.).
  • Commissioning of the system and synchronization with the grid.
  • Performance testing and generation verification.
  • Coordination with local DISCOM for net-meter installation and approval.
  • Obtaining all statutory clearances required for grid connectivity in Sikkim.
  • Handover of fully functional system to the beneficiary with demonstration.

D. Training, Documentation & After-Sales Support

  • Conduct beneficiary orientation / training on system operation, safety and basic upkeep.
  • Submit Installation Completion Report, As-built drawings, Test Certificates and Warranty documents for each site.
  • Provide 5 years of comprehensive maintenance / replacement guarantee for all equipment installed.
  • Maintain a local / regional service support mechanism for the defect-liability period.

E. Deliverables

  • Inception Report & Work Plan
  • Material Inspection / Dispatch Clearance Reports
  • Site-wise Installation Completion Certificates (signed by beneficiary & agency)
  • Commissioning & Performance Test Reports
  • Net-Metering Approval / Grid Connectivity Documents
  • Beneficiary Training Attendance & Completion Report
  • As-built Drawings & Technical Documentation (soft + hard copy)
  • Final Project Completion Report with photo documentation (GPS-tagged)
  • Warranty / Guarantee Cards and 5-year AMC commitment letter

F. Technical Specifications of 1 KW On-Grid Rooftop Solar System (Annexure-I)

The system shall conform to the following minimum specifications (reference from EOI / MNRE guidelines):

2Inverter / PCUSingle MPPT On-Grid Inverter of 1 kVA capacity, as per IEC standards1 No.EXIDE / UTL / Microtek or equivalent
3Interconnecting DC Cables1C × 4 sq mm 1.1 kV, PVC insulated, UV Protected Cu Cable (Array Connection)As per site requirementHPL / Polycab ISI certified

5Fasnut / FastenersM-10, 3" Stainless SteelAs per site requirementSS
6Conduit Pipe1" Heavy dutyAs per site requirementStandard Make

11AC Cable with Lugs4 Sq mm Copper wireAs per site requirementFinolex / KEI

Note: Convergence / Subsidy Amount under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is FIXED at INR 33,000 per 1 KW system. Bidder shall quote the total project cost; the convergence amount will be adjusted as per scheme guidelines.

4. Timeline

The entire assignment (supply, installation, commissioning and documentation of all 100 systems) shall be completed within 8 weeks from the date of the Work Order or handing over of the final list of surveyed / approved beneficiary sites, whichever is later. A detailed week-wise implementation schedule shall form part of the Technical Proposal.

5. Applicable Indian Compliance & Statutory Acts

Bidders must ensure all supply, installation, documentation and process workflows strictly comply with the following statutory requirements:

  • PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana guidelines and portal requirements issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) / implementing agencies.
  • Electricity Act, 2003 and relevant State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC) regulations for net-metering in Sikkim.
  • BIS / IEC standards applicable to Solar PV Modules, Inverters, Cables and Balance of System components.
  • Data Protection & Privacy norms applicable to household-level personal data collection.
  • GST & Tax Regulations: Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) and State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) compliance with valid GSTIN.
  • MSMED Act, 2006: Benefits applicable to registered Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) per Govt. of India directives.
  • Labor & Safety Laws: Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and applicable provisions for personnel involved during installation and commissioning.

6. Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for evaluation, a Bidder must satisfy all the following minimum eligibility conditions and furnish documentary proof in the Technical Bid:

  1. The Bidder shall be a legally constituted entity (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company, registered society or registered contractor) operating in India.
  2. The Bidder shall hold a valid Trade Licence and a valid GST Registration Certificate.
  3. The Bidder shall hold a valid PAN issued by the Income-tax Department.
  4. The Bidder should have satisfactorily executed similar rooftop solar supply / installation / commissioning assignments (minimum cumulative 50 kW or 50 systems) during the last three (03) financial years (supported by work orders and completion certificates).
  5. The Bidder should have an average annual financial turnover of at least INR 50,00,000 – 75,00,000 over the last three (3) financial years (supported by audited statements / CA certificate).
  6. The Bidder shall not be blacklisted, debarred or banned by any Central / State Government department, public sector undertaking, or funding agency as on the date of submission.
  7. The Bidder shall submit relevant work orders/purchase orders and completion certificates as evidence of successful execution of similar assignments.
  8. Preference may be given to bidders having demonstrated experience of working in Sikkim / North-Eastern Region and/or providing end-to-end support including supply, installation, net-metering, training and post-installation handholding.
  9. The Bidder shall have qualified electrical / solar engineers and a dedicated installation team capable of field deployment in Sikkim.
  10. The Bidder (or its OEM partners) should preferably be empanelled / registered under MNRE or State Nodal Agency for rooftop solar programmes.

Technical Proposal

PPHF intends to implement a CSR-Government convergence project for installation of 1 KW rooftop solar systems. The selected agency will conduct beneficiary identification, technical feasibility surveys, documentation, and portal support before installation.

Access to affordable electricity remains a challenge for deprived households. PPHF intends to implement a CSR-Government convergence project for installation of 1 KW rooftop solar systems under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for 100 eligible households in Sikkim.

2.2 Purpose

  • Upload of complete beneficiary details on the official PM Surya Ghar portal.

A. Machinery & Equipment

S. No. Equipment Particulars Detailed Specifications & Technical Requirements Required Units
1 Urli Roaster Stainless Steel (SS304 contact parts) roasting unit with 50–75 kg/batch capacity. LPG/Electric dual heating option, temp range 90–120°C with digital control panel. 1 Unit
2 Ribbon Blender 200 kg/batch capacity with motorized control panel. Food-grade SS304 blades and mixing drum for uniform spice/herbal blending. 1 Unit
3 Form Fill Seal Machine (Automatic) Automated FFS Packaging Machine for pouch capacities 100 g, 250 g, 500 g, and 1 kg. Speed: 1000–1500 pouches/hour. Equipped with batch coding and nitrogen flushing. 1 Unit
4 Pulveriser / Grinder 50–100 kg/hr capacity pulveriser with SS contact parts and pulse-jet dust collection system. Suitable for fine powder grinding of turmeric, ginger, chilli, etc. 1 Unit
5 Spice Sterilizer Steam-based/Thermal sterilization unit (100 kg/batch) for microbial load reduction to conform to FSSAI standards. 1 Unit
6 Weighing & Sealing Units Electronic digital precision scale (up to 10 kg) and heavy-duty continuous band sealer for manual backup packaging. 1 Set

B. Solar Utility & Civil Integration

  • Solar Backup System: Supply and installation of an off-grid/hybrid solar power backup system tailored to run essential machinery load (1000–1200 sq. ft shed setup).

C. Human Resources, Training, Operational Deliverables & Market Linkage

  • Skilled Machine Operators: Provision/engagement support for 04 trained local youth for 1 month of setup and commissioning.

SUBJECT: Invitation of quotation for Impact Assessment of SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels(Rajasthan)

You are invited tosubmit your most competitive quotation for the following make as per the units mentioned in TOR. The standard forms in this RFP may be retyped for completion, but the bidder is responsible for their accurate reproduction.

1 Background and Context Access to primary healthcare remains a persistent challenge in geographically remote and underserved regions of India, where physical distance, limited infrastructure, and socio-economic barriers constrain timely care-seeking. The SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels is a flagship mobile healthcare initiative implemented by People to People Health Foundation (PPHF), with support from SBI Foundation and SBI Cap Securities. The programme operates across 40 villages in Kishanganj and Shahabad blocks of Baran district, Rajasthan, delivering doorstep primary healthcare services through Mobile Medical Units (MMUs).

The intervention integrates:

  • Mobile Outpatient Department (MOPD) services

  • Preventive and diagnostic screening

  • Referral linkages to higher facilities

  • Community awareness and behaviour change activities

  • Thematic health and Swachh Bharat camps

The programme is designed not only to improve service delivery but also to strengthen early detection, promote preventive health behaviours, and enhance linkages with the public health system.

Purpose of the Assignment

PPHF seeks to conduct an independent impact assessment to generate robust, evidence-based insights on the

programme’s effectiveness, outcomes, and implementation model. The assessment is expected to:

  • Rigorously evaluate programme performance against its intended objectives

  • Assess the extent of change attributable to the intervention

  • Identify scalable elements and operational efficiencies

  • Generate strategic recommendations for programme strengthening and replication

Objectives of the Assessment

The assessment will address the following core objectives:

  • Programme Reach and Equity

      • Assess the extent and inclusiveness of programme coverage

      • Examine reach among vulnerable and underserved populations

  • Access and Utilization of Healthcare Services

      • Evaluate changes in access to primary healthcare services

      • Assess utilization patterns of MMU services

  • Health Awareness and Behaviour Change

      • Measure changes in awareness of key health issues

      • Assess adoption of preventive and health-seeking behaviours

  • Early Detection and Continuum of Care

      • Evaluate effectiveness of screening services

      • Assess referral uptake, completion, and follow-through

      • Examine linkages with public health systems

  • Service Quality and Beneficiary Experience

      • Assess perceived quality, trust, and acceptability of services

      • Measure beneficiary satisfaction

  • Programme Efficiency and Implementation Effectiveness

  1. Analyse operational design and delivery efficiency

  2. Identify implementation strengths, bottlenecks, and innovations

  • Sustainability and Scalability

    • Assess the sustainability of the intervention model

    • Identify potential for scale-up and replication

Scope of Work

The selected agency will undertake a comprehensive, mixed-methods evaluation covering the following:

  1. Evaluation Design

  2. Methodology

  3. Sampling Strategy

  4. Data Analysis

Deliverables

The agency will be responsible for the following deliverables:

  1. Inception Report

  2. Data Collection Instruments

  3. Fieldwork Completion Brief

  4. Draft Impact Assessment Report

  5. Final Report

  6. Presentation

  7. Data Outputs

Timeline

The assignment is expected to be completed within 4-8 weeks:

Phase

Timeline

Inception, Design, Tool Finalization

1 Week

Data Collection

2 weeks

Analysis & Reporting

1 week

Team Composition and Expertise

The agency should demonstrate:

  • Proven experience in public health evaluations

  • Prior work in rural and underserved geographies

  • Expertise in mixed-methods research and impact evaluation

Ethical Considerations

  • Informed consent from all participants

  • Confidentiality and data protection protocols

  • Adherence to ethical research standards

Governance and Reporting

The selected agency will report to PPHF and engage closely with programme stakeholders. Periodic review meetings will be conducted to ensure quality, alignment, and timely delivery.

Proposal Submission Requirements

Interested agencies are required to submit:

  • Technical and Financial Proposal

    • Understanding of the assignment

    • Detailed methodology and approach

    • Work plan and timelines

  • Organizational Profile

Payment Terms

Payments will be linked to key deliverables, typically:

  • 50 % before Inception Report approval

  • 30 % Submission of Draft Report

  • 20% Final Report

  • Minimum 5 years of organizational experience.

  • At least 3 similar impact assessment assignments completed in the last 5 years.

  • Experience working with CSR, public health, or development sector projects.

  • Availability of qualified researchers and statisticians.

  • PAN, GST, and registration certificates.

PPHF/5031/26-27/Social Events

Expression of Interest (EoI)
Ref. No.: PPHF/5031/26-27/Social Events
Date: 10th June 2026

Project/Site Location: West Sikkim, Sikkim

Background & Rationale

Community-level social events are an effective, low-cost and participatory channel for delivering health and social messages directly to target groups. By combining interactive learning with recognition and engagement activities, such events achieve higher recall of key messages and encourage community ownership.

Each event is designed for a focused group of 25–30 trainees / participants, a size that allows meaningful interaction, hands-on participation and effective dissemination of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials.

Objectives

  • Raise awareness on the targeted health / social theme among community members.
  • Engage participants through interactive and participatory methods that aid retention of key messages.
  • Distribute IEC materials and handouts to reinforce learning beyond the event.
  • Encourage positive behaviour change and community ownership of the issue.

Scope of Activities (Per Event)

  • Mobilization and registration of 25–30 trainees / participants from the target community.
  • Set-up of the event venue with a branded informational banner.
  • Distribution of IEC materials and handouts carrying the key messages.
  • Conduct of an interactive Question–Answer session and a Painting Competition to drive engagement and learning.
  • Recognition of participants through prizes, kits, chocolates and gifts.
  • Documentation of the event (attendance, photographs and a brief report).

Methodology & Event Components

Banner

A branded banner displaying the event theme and key messages is installed at the venue to anchor the event and reinforce visibility.

IEC Materials / Hand-outs

Printed leaflets, pamphlets and handouts are distributed to each participant so that key messages can be revisited and shared within households after the event.

Question–Answer Session / Painting Competition

An interactive Q&A session tests and reinforces understanding, while a painting competition offers a creative, participatory way for participants to express and internalize the messages.

Prizes / Kits / Gifts

Participants and winners are recognized with prizes, kits, and small gifts, which encourage participation and create a positive association with the messages delivered.

Implementation & Monitoring

PPHF will plan and execute each event in coordination with the local community and relevant stakeholders. Monitoring will be carried out through attendance records, participant feedback, event photographs and a brief completion report submitted after each event.

Expected Outcomes

  • Improved awareness and understanding of the targeted theme among 25–30 participants per event.
  • Wider message reach through IEC materials carried back into households.
  • Higher community engagement and willingness to adopt recommended practices.

  • Measurement verification.
  • Workmanship inspection.
  • Safety compliance monitoring.

Supervision Reports Weekly

html:
Supply, Installation and Commissioning of Digital Mammography System , District Hospital, Jhajjar

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL

Purchaser: People to People Health Foundation (PPHF)

Contract Title: Supply, Installation and Commissioning of Digital Mammography System , District Hospital, Jhajjar

RFQ No.: PPHF/RFQ/5051/01

S.No Description Date & Time
1 Date ofIssue of RFP 10 th March 2026
2 LastDate and Time of submission of RFPs 13 th March 2026 at 17:30 Hrs
3 Opening ofRFPs 14 th March 2026

Introduction:
People to People Health Foundation (PPHF) invites sealed quotations from eligible vendors for supply,delivery, installation and commissioning of Digital Mammography for District Hospital at Jhajjar, as per the details provided in Annexure 1 and Annexure 2 (attached below) Interested bidders are requested to submit their most competitive quotation in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in this RFQ document. The formats provided in the RFQ may be reproduced by bidders for submission; however, bidders shall ensure that the reproduced documents are accurate and complete.

Scope of Work:
The selected vendor shall be responsible for the following:
• Supply of equipment as per the specifications provided in the RFQ.
• Delivery of the items to the designated location.
• Installation and commissioning
• Providing necessary manuals, documentation, and warranties as applicable.

The place of installation and commissioning will be at District Hospital, Jhajjar.

Terms and Conditions
1. Eligibility: A Bidder(s) shall not participate in more than one Quotation; (b) shall not have conflict of interest as defined in the PPHF’s Procurement Policies; and (c) should not have been blacklisted or suspended by Central or any State Government Departments in India

2. Clarifications & Amendments: If the Purchaser/Vendor receives any request for clarification of this RFQ Document, it will publish together with any amendment to this document, on www.pphfglobal.org for information of all Bidders. Bidders should regularly check on the website, for any amendments to the terms and conditions.

3. Quotation Price
a) The bidder must specify the unit being offered. The quantity offered should be 100% of the required amount including all transportation, installation, and applicable taxes. Any corrections must be made by crossing out the error, initialing, dating, and rewriting the correct information.
b) Quotation should be placed in a single sealed envelope (Hard Copy) or soft copy to procurement@pphfglobal.org, clearly subject marked as “Quotation for Digital
Mammography System for District Hospital Jhajjar, RFQ No.PPHF/RFQ/5051/01
c) All duties, taxes and other levies payable on the components shall be included in the total price.
d) Goods and Service Tax (GST) should be indicated separately.
e) The rates quoted by the bidder shall be fixed for the duration of the contract/purchase
order and shall not be subject to adjustment on any account.
f) The Prices shall be quoted in Indian Rupees only (INR).
g) Bidder must expressly mention the Name/Brand/Model No and any other extra
specifications/configurations etc. of the items offered by them in the price schedule along with proper brochures. Specification Brochures should be submitted along with the bid.
h) The bidder must mention in detail about the product being offered in lieu of the specified specifications and not by simply mentioning “Complied”. Quotations with no proper technical specifications/catalogues are likely to be disqualified.

4. Qualification of Bidders
a) Have the legal capacity to enter into a contract.
b) Not be insolvent, in receivership, bankrupt or being wound up or subject to legal proceedings for any of these circumstances.
c) Not have had the business activities suspended or debarred from public procurement by the State Government or Government of India.
d) Not have any conflict of Interest with any PPHF or any associate personnel.

5. Documents Evidencing Qualification: Bidders are requested to submit copies of the following documents as evidence of your qualification.
a) Valid trading license/registration or equivalent/Exemption Certificate.
b) Valid certificate of GST registration.
c) Valid bank details (Passbook copy/cancelled cheque)
d) MSME certificate (If applicable).
e) PAN (Mandatory for all entities) and AADHAAR (For proprietors only).
f) Self-declaration that the bidder’s business activities are not suspended or debarred from public procurement by the Government of India.

6. Validity of Quotation: Quotations shall remain valid for a period not less than 30 days after the deadline date specified for submission.

7. Evaluation of Quotations: The Purchaser will evaluate and compare the quotations unit wise that are determined to be substantially responsive i.e. which
a) Are properly on letterhead (Mentioned Name, Address, GST no, PAN no.) with signed and stamp on each page.
b) Properly mentioned Document ref number, date and subject
c) Confirm the terms and conditions and specifications.
d) The Quotations would be evaluated unit wise; GST will be taken into consideration while evaluating the quotations.
e) Any historical information, if required, may be asked of the bidders during evaluation of quotes.
f) Make sure in the quotation, mention brand, model, make details of materials… Ensure popular branded items are used for Medical Equipment.

These videos are intended to communicate simple, actionable health messages in an engaging format, suitable for digital platforms, community outreach, and health facility settings.

  • Objective

The objective of this assignment is to conceptualize, produce, and deliver three short videos that promote early action, healthier lifestyles, and risk reduction related to obesity, excessive screen time, and tobacco use, with messaging tailored for different population groups.

  • Scope of Work

The selected agency / production partner shall be responsible for the end-to-end production of three 60-second videos, including concept development, scripting, visual design, animation or live-action filming (as applicable), voice-over, editing, and final delivery.

Video 1: Animated – “Obesity Is More Than Weight”

Theme: Obesity and early risk identification

Format: Animated video

Target Audience: General population

Key Messages:

  • Excess body weight acts as a silent trigger and increases the risk of multiple diseases
  • Obesity is linked to diabetes, heart disease, hypertension, and other NCDs
  • Early action can prevent complications
  • Call to action: Measure. Screen. Act Early.

Scope Includes:

  • Development of a clear, animation-led visual narrative
  • Simple, non-technical messaging suitable for wide audiences
  • Strong emphasis on early screening and preventive action
  • Voice-over and visuals aligned with public health messaging
  • Duration: 60 seconds

Theme: Screen time, physical inactivity, and lifestyle risk

Target Audience: Children, adolescents, and young adults

  • Youth increasingly consumed by social media, gaming, and doom scrolling
  • Excessive screen time contributes to physical inactivity, obesity, poor posture, eye strain, and mental fatigue
  • Prolonged screen exposure increases the long-term risk of NCDs
  • Simple lifestyle changes such as screen breaks, outdoor play, and daily physical activity improve overall health

Scope Includes:

  • Contemporary visuals reflecting youth behavior and digital habits
  • Relatable scenarios showing both problem and solution
  • Positive framing without blame or moralizing
  • Clear, achievable actions promoted through visuals and narration
  • Duration: 60 seconds

  • Tobacco use impacts not only the user but also family members and loved ones

As part of its Behavior Change Communication (BCC) activities, Project PRANAA proposes the development of three Kannada audio-visual jingles to promote regular health screening, discourage tobacco use, and encourage healthier dietary practices among different population groups.

  • Objective

The objective of this assignment is to conceptualize, produce, and deliver three Kannada jingles with accompanying videos that convey clear public health messages and encourage positive behavior change related to NCD prevention and control.

  • Scope of Work

The selected agency / production partner will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of three Kannada audio-visual jingles. This will include creative conceptualization, lyric writing, music composition, audio recording, video production, editing, and final delivery.

Jingle 1: “Love Yourself – Get Regular Screening Done”

Theme: Early detection and preventive health

Target Audience: Adult population (urban and rural)

Key Messages:

  • Several NCDs remain asymptomatic in their early stages

  • Delayed detection can lead to serious and life-threatening complications

  • Regular health screening should be adopted as a routine practice

Scope Includes:

  • Development of Kannada lyrics using simple and relatable language

  • Composition of an emotion-driven melody that reinforces self-care and responsibility

  • Video narrative depicting individuals opting for routine health screening

  • Subtle reference to government or public health screening services

  • Duration: 30–45 seconds

Jingle 2: “Smoking / Vaping Is Not Cool”

Theme: Tobacco control and youth empowerment

Target Audience: Adolescents and young adults

Key Messages:

  • Smoking, vaping, and tobacco use are harmful and should not be normalized

  • Tobacco consumption leads to cancer, heart disease, diabetes, and lung disorders

  • Young people should be encouraged to resist peer pressure and make informed choices

Creative Approach:

  • Use of rap elements blended with popular Kannada folk rhythms

  • Energetic and youth-centric presentation

  • Visuals highlighting confidence, sports, creativity, and positive refusal

Scope Includes:

  • Youth-friendly Kannada lyrics with strong, memorable lines

  • Original composition combining rap and folk music styles

  • Contemporary visuals reflecting youth culture

  • Duration: 30–45 seconds

Jingle 3: “Healthy Aahara – Healthy Jeevana”

Theme: Nutrition and healthy lifestyle

Target Audience: Families, women, and general population

Key Messages:

  • Reduction in consumption of junk food and sugary beverages

  • Promotion of reading food labels and mindful eating habits

  • Encouragement of local, seasonal, and home-cooked food practices

Scope Includes:

  • Kannada lyrics rooted in local culture and familiarity

  • Warm and positive musical tone highlighting traditional food values

  • Visuals featuring local kitchens, markets, and family settings

  • Positioning food choices as a preventive health measure

  • Duration: 30–45 seconds

  • Deliverables

  • Final Kannada audio jingle (studio-quality)

  • High-quality video (Full HD; suitable for television and digital platforms)

Particular Unit
Fixed Cost

Terms of Reference (ToR)

Rapid Baseline Assessment

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF) is hiring an individual consultant or an agency to conduct a Rapid Baseline Assessment for the project titled “Identifying Gaps in Early Identification and Management of High-Risk Pregnancies”

Section A

About Us

PPHF, a public health non-profit organization, works towards transforming lives for improved health and wellbeing through locally- driven solutions. PPHF work closely with communities and key actors on sustainable solutions for public health challenges.

Background

The urban poor in India represent the most vulnerable section of the population in terms of the health outcomes. They experience significant disparities in access to quality healthcare, including immunization, antenatal care, skilled deliveries, and newborn care. Rapid urbanization has led to an increase in informal settlements, where healthcare access is limited and awareness is low.

According to NFHS-5, the prevalence of High-Risk Pregnancies (HRP) in Karnataka is 46.5%, signaling an urgent need to strengthen systems for early identification, referral, and management of HRPs to prevent adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.

In this context, PPHF, in collaboration with the Municipal Corporation of Bangalore and the ESIC administration, is implementing a project to support the government’s efforts to improve timely and effective care for high-risk pregnant women. The initiative seeks to leverage existing government schemes such as NHM, ESIC, and Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) to enhance maternal health outcomes among the urban poor.

The project will be implemented in Anandapuram Urban Slum, located in KR Market Ward, Bangalore Central.

Project Goal: To enhance the tracking of high-risk pregnancies (HRP) for the early identification of potential complications, facilitating timely interventions and specialized care for improved maternal and newborn health outcomes in Anandapuram (a Bangalore slum)

Section B

About Rapid Need Assessment

The Rapid Baseline Assessment aims to identify the gaps in the early identification, referral, and management of high-risk pregnancies among the urban poor population of Anandapuram. It will assess system readiness, service delivery mechanisms, and barriers to treatment adherence, while identifying opportunities to strengthen government and community linkages.

Objectives of the Assessment

1. Identify Gaps in the early identification of high-risk pregnancies at the community and facility levels.

2. Assess System Capacity to provide timely and adequate treatment for HRPs through NHM and ESIC frameworks.

3. Examine Dropouts and Non-Adherence: Understand the socio-cultural, behavioral, and system-related factors leading to discontinuation of antenatal care.

4. Map Government and Partner Schemes: Identify existing state and national maternal health schemes and referral pathways to explore convergence opportunities.

5. Recommend Strategies for improving HRP tracking, referral efficiency, and treatment adherence.

Scope of Work

The selected consultant or agency will be responsible for the following tasks:

1) Desk Review

· Review state and national-level policies and guidelines on maternal health and HRP management (NHM, ESIC, PMSMA).

· Analyze secondary data sources such as NFHS, HMIS, and local facility-level records.

· Review referral mechanisms and data management systems currently in use.

2) Field Assessment

· Conduct Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with:

o Municipal Health Officials (BBMP, NHM, ESIC)

o Medical officers, ANMs, ASHAs, and community health workers

o Pregnant women, family members, and dropout cases

· Assess facility-level capacities (infrastructure, HR, diagnostics, referral systems).

· Document challenges and enablers in service delivery and referral mechanisms.

3) Data Analysis and Reporting

· Analyze qualitative and quantitative data to identify gaps and bottlenecks.

· Develop a comprehensive report with actionable recommendations to improve HRP identification, follow-up, and treatment adherence.

· Present findings in a validation workshop with key stakeholders.

Timelines: Approximately 6–8 weeks from the date of contract signing.

Deliverables:

· Detailed study protocol including data collectors training, field supervision plan and data

· Data Collection tools

· Draft report

· Final report

· Summary report

· PPT on the summary report

Qualifications and Experience

For Individual Consultant:

· Postgraduate degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, or Health Management.

· Minimum 5-7 years of experience in conducting health systems or maternal health assessments.

· Experience in qualitative research and community-based data collection, fluency in Kannada language.

For Consulting Firm:

· The Agency should be a registered body (proprietary, partnership firm, company/ society/ trust) NGO and academic institute.

· Proven experience in conducting baseline or impact assessments in maternal or urban health.

· A multidisciplinary team with expertise in public health research, data analysis, and field operations.

· Demonstrated experience working with government health departments or development partners in Karnataka or similar contexts.

Application Procedure

Interested individual consultants or firms are invited to submit:

1. Technical Proposal: detailing understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, work plan, and team composition.

2. Financial Proposal: inclusive of professional fees, travel, and taxes. The financial proposal shall cover the itemized/ day wise cost and the total cost based on the ToR. Payments will be made in instalments based on deliverables as specified in this ToR.

3. Profile/CVs of key personnel or individual consultant.

4. Samples of similar assignments conducted in the last three years.

PPHF point of contact: Dr Nalini Kaushik, Technical Advisor

Send your application to procurement@pphfglobal.org wth the subject line:
“EOI – Rapid Baseline Assessment on High-Risk Pregnancy – Anandapuram, Bangalore” by 10th November 2025.

html:
Scope of Work for Conducting Baseline Assessment : Project Punaraya

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL

Implementing Agency: People to People Health Foundation (PPHF)
Study Period: Aug– September 2025

1. Project Background and Rationale

The Project Punaraya aims to cover the whole spectrum of service delivery components i.e., infrastructure, equipment, motivation, skills, monitoring, and increasing demand from the community side thereon access to quality health services having the focus on the target group of maternal & child health and adolescent health. The project would have equal weightage to all components and cross-cutting factors that are directly connected to overall quality service delivery.

At the beginning of the project, it is planned to conduct a comprehensive health profile assessment to understand the health challenges and service gaps in the selected geography. This assessment will identify prevalent health issues, including communicable and non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health concerns, and nutritional deficiencies. It will also evaluate the availability, quality, and accessibility of primary healthcare services, including essential medicines, diagnostics, and referral systems. The assessment will further explore risky health behaviours such as tobacco use, alcohol consumption, and delays in seeking care, alongside barriers to accessing formal healthcare services. Based on these findings, actionable recommendations will be developed to address gaps, improve health behaviours, and strengthen healthcare infrastructure.

  1. Objectives of the assessment
    • Conduct a baseline health facility assessment to map existing services, gaps, and resource requirements.
    • Assess community health concerns related to anemia, maternal, child and adolescent health, and non-communicable diseases (NCDs).
    • Come up with evidence-based recommendations to increase footfall and utilization of health services.
  1. Scope of Work
  2. Geography of the assessment:

  2. Bazrapara AAM (Ayushman Arogya Mandir)-under Kamrup (Rural)-Rampur Block

  • Review of service availability (maternal & child health, adolescent health, NCD screening, anemia management, etc.).

  • Household surveys on health-seeking behavior and practices.

Endline Study for the 1st phase of the project SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL

Purchaser: People to People Health Foundation (PPHF)

Contract title: Endline Study for the 1st phase of the project SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels

S. No. Description Date & Time
1 Date of Issue of RFP 04-May-25
2 Last Date and Time of submission of RFPs 11 May 2025, at 17:30 Hrs.
3 Opening of RFPs 13 May 2025, at 17:30 Hrs..

Scope of Work for Conducting Endline Study
Project: SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels (1st Phase)
Implementing Agency: People to People Health Foundation (PPHF)
Study Period: May– June 2025

  1. Background

The SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels project, implemented by PPHF, aims to provide primary and preventive healthcare services through Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) across selected rural and underserved districts of Odisha: Nuapada, Balangir, and Dhenkanal. Over a 15-month period, the project is being implemented with a target to improve access to healthcare services and enhance health outcomes through healthcare delivery, awareness sessions, and specialized health camps.

PPHF seeks a qualified agency to undertake an Endline Study for the 1st phase of the project to assess the performance, outcomes, and impact of the project compared to the baseline, and to document lessons for future replication or scale-up.

  1. Objectives of the Endline Study
  • To assess the availability and accessibility of services provided by the Mobile Medical Units
  • To assess the awareness generated by the Mobile Medical Units
  • To assess the effect of Mobile Medical Units on health care services seeking of community
  1. Scope of Work

The selected agency shall undertake the following tasks:

A. Desk Review and Inception

  • Review project documents, baseline/ Village Health Assessment report, implementation plans, monitoring reports.
  • Conduct meetings with PPHF’s project management team.
  • Finalize study design, methodology, sampling strategy, and tools.

B. Data Collection

  • Quantitative Surveys: Household-level surveys with project beneficiaries across the three districts
  • Qualitative Methods: Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) with:
    • Pregnant/lactating women
    • Elderly and adolescent groups
    • MMU staff, ASHAs, ANMs
    • Health department officials

C. Data Analysis

  • Compare results against baseline/ project indicators
  • Analyze service utilization trends, referral linkages, and impact on health behaviour
  • Identify gaps, strengths, and unintended outcomes

D. Reporting

  • Draft Report: Presentation to PPHF for validation.
  • Final Report: Incorporate feedback, include executive summary, data tables, case studies, and conclusions.
  1. Deliverables
Deliverable Timeline
Inception Report (design, tools, sample size) By 12th June 2025
Data Collection & Analysis Plan Within 1 and half week
Draft Endline Report By 28th June 2025
Final Endline Report with Annexures By end of June 2025
  1. Methodology

The agency is expected to adopt a mixed-methods approach:

  • Quantitative: Cross-sectional surveys, pre/post comparisons
  • Qualitative: Narrative inquiry, document stakeholder’s perception
  • EMR/OPD registers may be used as secondary sources where applicable; project team may support the agency in providing such type of data
  1. Qualifications of the Agency/Consultant
  • Proven experience in public health research / studies/ evaluations
  • Qualified team with expertise in public health and research/ studies
  • Prior work with CSR-funded or government-aligned health programs is desirable
  1. Timeline

The study must be completed within 4 weeks from the date of signing the agreement.

  1. Budget

Interested agencies/Consultant should submit a financial proposal (in INR) inclusive of all field costs, personnel, travel, data processing, and reporting.

  1. Proposal Submission Requirements
  • Organizational/Consultant profile with credentials of health projects and research/ studies
  • Financial Proposal
  • GST and PAN details and other basic prerequisites

RFA for Rapid Formative Research (Jhajjar District, Haryana)

Scope of Work

Background: PPHF is a health organization, working with a mission of transforming lives for improved health and wellbeing through locally driven solutions. We are registered as non-for-profit company under section 8 in India. (https://pphfglobal.org/)

About PPHF: People to People Health Foundation (PPHF) is a non-profit organization committed to strengthening public health in India through research, education, and policy advocacy. PPHF, in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) CiBioD and the Government of India, is implementing a project to enhance primary healthcare services through Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs).

Project Overview: The project aims to install AI-powered health kiosks in selected Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in aspirational and low-performing districts. This initiative is designed to facilitate early diagnosis, treatment, and referral for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), reduce morbidity and mortality from NCDs, improve health access for female beneficiaries, and reduce government health expenditure. The project also includes training frontline workers and generating awareness through health camps.

PPHF intends to conduct qualitative assessments on the status of NCD and 12 essential services in selected district – PHCs and CHCs in Jhajjar. PPHF, invites proposal from the eligible and competent agencies for the Rapid formative Research (RFA).

Objective of the Rapid Formative Research:

The intended RFA is aimed to contribute to and design and develop specific interventions to improve the service delivery of NCDs and 12 essential services under PMJAY. The assessment will identify the factors that restrain or enable NCD and essential services related provisions, supply, problems, perceptions, beliefs, awareness, practices, and other related issues (system and community) in the selected project area.

The key objectives of the formative research are:

  1. To undertake rapid formative assessments with clients and providers for services with focus on the situation at selected PHCs, CHCs and Districts.
  2. To prepare detailed reports for the rapid formative assessments.
  3. To prepared a summary 4 pager document that gives overview of the methodology, key challenges identified and recommendations.
  4. Summary PowerPoint presentation on the finding and recommendations of the RFA.

Key Activities:

Conduct a desk review of relevant existing practices, documents, guidelines, plans, policies, materials, and literature across at the national and state level.

  1. Interact with key stakeholders at facility level; using qualitative methodologies (IDIs).
  2. Conduct FGDs and In-depth interviews with the community.
  3. Conduct NCD stakeholders mapping in the state.
  4. Digital technology and Supply chain mapping-Conduct observational visits in field for assessing current practices in supply chain management on NCDs.
  5. Understand data recording and tracking under HMIS and its integration under ABDM and PMJAY
  6. Understand the efficiency, capacity of the PHC to deliver the essential services and capture the utilisation of services
  7. Identify gaps/needs for improving the program service delivery and uptake.
  8. Prepare concrete documentation of the key findings.
  9. Select a representative sample of PHCs in the district to implement Health Facility assessment and their ratings as per Kayakalp.

Methodology

The assessment will be carried out at two levels: communities and systems. Both secondary and primary data shall be utilized. The assessment will involve qualitative methods using In-depth Interviews (IDIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and stakeholder analysis, mapping and supply chain management on NCDs.

Time Frame and Plan: one month (including final report)

The Eligibility Conditions:

  • The Agency should be a registered body (proprietary, partnership firm, company/society/trust) NGO and academic institute or a team of epidemiologists with experience in Public Health and Health Statistics
  • The Agency should be in existence for at least one-two year and have experience in research and evaluation.

Introduction

People to People Health Foundation (PPHF), is a section 8 not-for-profit company in India. Our mission is to transform lives for improved health and well-being through locally driven solutions. Working with Ministry of Health and private sectors in India to address the program implementation gaps in key public health domains such as 1) Women, Adolescent and Child health;2) Nutrition; 3) Non-Communicable Diseases;4) Infectious Diseases; 5) Environmental Health

PPHF is implementing 2 MMU under Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels project in Kishanganj and Shahabad Block of Baran District, Rajasthan. The project ‘SBI Sanjeevani Clinic on Wheels’ aims to provide door-step health services to hard-to-reach communities by providing early detection of serious illnesses and increasing community awareness.

Sr. No. Process step Timeline/Details
1 Publication date of the RFP May 9, 2024
2 Response to the clarifications requested through email. May 10, 2024
3 Last Date and Time for submission of proposals May 14, 2024
4 Communication to shortlisted participants to make presentations May 15, 2024
5 Final communication of selection May 15, 2024
6 Submission of Proposals (Physical copies) May 16, 2024

PPHF is inviting proposals from prominent research organizations/ individuals to conduct the following.

  1. To measure the effect of clinic on wheels program on health care seeking behavior, practices and service utilization pattern in service villages (40)

Objective:

  • To measure the performance of MMUs against the program deliverable
  • To assess the change in health service care seeking pattern
  • To assess the perceived benefit and effect created by different services provided by MMU Ex, OPD services, Awareness session, Special Health Camp and Promoting Swachata Abhiyan

Methodology

The assessment will be carried out at two levels: communities and systems. Both secondary and primary data shall be utilized. The assessment will involve qualitative methods using In-depth Interviews (IDIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and secondary data and program data.

Geography: Kishanganj and Shahabad Block , Baran, Rajasthan

Request for Quotation (RFP)- Situational Analysis with TNA report (Selected PHC/HSC) – Bengaluru Rural (PPHF/RFP/23-24/024 )

Prepared By:
People to People Health Foundation
K-40, 3rd Floor, Jangpura Extension, South-East Delhi, Delhi – 110 014
connect@pphfglobal.org
www.pphfglobal.org

S. No.

Description

Date & Time

01

Date of Issue of RFP

31 January 2024

02

Last Date and Time of submission of RFPs

7 Feb 24, at 17:30 Hrs.

03

Opening of RFPs

8 Feb 24, at 17:30 Hrs..

Scope for Work

In the second phase, PPHF is implementing Project PRANAA with the state and local authorities at 3 upgraded PHCs of Bengaluru in Karnataka, to meet the unmet needs of NCDs for underprivileged population. This program is being implemented by PPHF in Karnataka with support from GE Healthcare to leverage the ongoing efforts on NCD program at the HWC/CHC level and strengthening the NCD service delivery further through community awareness and mobilization, upskilling of health care workers for early NCD screening, diagnosis, and management.

Under this initiative PPHF is inviting proposal from interested subject matter experts, research firm for below Task,

Task: To conduct Training need assessment with situational analysis for Project sites in Bangalore under Project PRANAA.

This will present a detailed baseline report offering a snapshot of the current scenario. It shall serve as a benchmark for assessing the impact and effectiveness of interventions under project PRANAA. Conducting a Training Needs Assessment (TNA) proves beneficial in discerning the training requirements of the target group. It is imperative to comprehend the present situation and pinpoint areas requiring enhancement or addressing gaps through capacity-building initiatives.

Objectives:

  • To understand the community needs, awareness level, beliefs, behaviors-practices and overall perceptions on NCDs.
  • To explore various factors (both demand and supply side) affecting service delivery on NCDs.
  • To understand training needs, knowledge, and capacity of the health Professionals on prevention and management of NCDs

Geographical Focus:

Bangalore: Avalahalli PHC, Doddatumkur PHC, and Siddhapura PHC

Deliverables:

  • Baseline Report with detailed TNA: A comprehensive baseline report will be produced, offering a detailed snapshot, which will act as a benchmark to measure the intervention’s impact and effectiveness.
  • Report to have detailed methodology and data collection tools.
  • Report to be converted to for short research article for publication.

Timeline: One month, Report to be submitted on 28 Feb 24

If you are interested submit your interest via email on connect@pphfglobal.org with a concept note for the same before 7 Feb 24. If you are applying at individual level kindly submit the CV with expected fees.

Introduction

PEOPLE TO PEOPLE HEALTH FOUNDATION (PPHF) is a non-government organization committed to transforming lives for improved health and wellbeing through locally driven solutions. PPHF have been working with Ministry of Health and private sectors in India to address the health program and policy implementation gaps. PPHF has very intensive experience in building capacity of health system and mobilize community for uptake of better health services. PPHF provides technical support on quality public health delivery, capacity strengthening and health technology. Besides that, PPHF generate new knowledge through implementation and demonstration for better programming and scaling up and has expressed its willingness to act as implementation partner in the execution of the Project.

1 Publication date of the RFQ 20th January 2023
2 Response to the clarifications requested through email. 23rd January 2023
3 Last Date and Time for submission of proposals 27th January 2023

5 Final communication of selection 28th January 2023

*Subject to all stakeholders complying with the defined timelines as per ownership/responsibility. The process will be completed in an online mode.

Instructions to the Agencies

1. Re-submission of Proposal

a. The agency can only submit one proposal at a time.

2. Completeness of Response:
a. The agencies are requested to study all instructions, forms, terms, requirements and other information in the RFQ document carefully (including BOQ Format). The proposal should be strictly based on the attached BOQ format. Submission of the proposal shall be deemed to have been done after careful study and examination of the RFQ document with full understanding of its implications.
b. The response to this RFQ should be complete in all respect. Failure to furnish all information required by the RFQ documents or submission of a proposal not substantially responsive to the RFQ documents in every respect will be at the agency’s risk and may result in the rejection of its proposal.

3. Agency Inquiries/Clarifications:
a. The agency shall send their queries to connect@pphfglobal.org with the subject PPHF PHC Medical Equipment – RFQ, before the due date for submission of queries/clarifications as mentioned in the key events and dates.
b. Queries on the telephone, social media, or any other medium will NOT be entertained.
c. PPHF will facilitate, in case the agency wishes to visit the site for assessment.

4. PPHF’s right to terminate the process:
a. PPHF may terminate the RFQ process at any time and without assigning any reason thereof.
b. PPHF reserves the right to amend/edit/add/delete any clause. However, this will be informed to all and will become part of the RFQ.
c. During the RFQ process, if any information is found false/ fraudulent/ mala fide, then PPHF shall reject the proposal and if necessary, initiate appropriate action.

5. Language of Proposal:
a. Proposals should be submitted in English language only.

6. Documents (Scan) to be submitted and Pre-qualification criteria:
a. The Agency should be an agency registered in India.

Documents to be submitted: Certificate of Incorporation/Registration, PAN Card, GST Certificate, Previous Work Experience Certificate & Related Reports.

b. The Agency will be expected to have a minimum experience of 5 years in a similar area.

c. The Agency should not have been blacklisted by any Government Agency/PSU/Central/State agency or under a declaration of ineligibility for fraudulent or corrupt practices.

Documents to be submitted: Declaration from the currently authorized signatory of the company.

7. Evaluation Process:
a. PPHF will shortlist the proposals based on the Shortlisting criteria.
b. Internal Committee of PPHF shall evaluate the shortlisted proposals based on procurement policy.

8. Penalty
a. PPHF shall be at liberty to impose penalties, including cancellation of the contract if the agency indulges in fraudulent activities, malpractices and male fides.

9. Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
a. Selected agencies will have to sign the Non-Disclosure Agreement (Annexure) with PPHF.

10. Sub-Contracting of Agreement or Purchase Order
a. The requested assignment can’t be assigned or subcontracted to another agency.

11. Proposal Preparation Costs
a. The agency shall submit the proposal at its own cost and PPHF shall not be held responsible for any cost incurred by the agency. Submission of a proposal does not entitle the agency to claim any cost and rights over PPHF and PPHF shall be at liberty to cancel any or all proposals without giving any notice. All materials submitted by the agencies shall be the absolute property of PPHF and no copyright/patent, etc. shall be entertained by PPHF.

12. PPHF’s right to terminate the process
a. PPHF may terminate the RFQ process at any time and without assigning any reason thereof. PPHF reserves the right to amend/edit/add/delete any clause of this Proposal Document. However, this will be informed to all and will become part of the RFQ.

13. Submission of Proposals
The proposal submission shall comprise of the duly filled as per BOQ format attached with RFQ.

14. Late Proposals
Any proposals received by PPHF after the deadline for submission of proposal shall be declared late and will be rejected and returned unopened to the agency at the discretion of PPHF.

PPHF shall award the contract to the selected /identified agency at its own discretion.

1. EXPECTATIONS FROM THE BIDDERS

  • • The Agency will report to the Activity Manager and will work directly with the PPHF team. The agency is required to depute a resource person for day-to-day work/updates and revisions.
  • • The agency will help the team by working at shorter deadlines. A prior experience of working with Government institutions is preferred. The agency is expected to have flexibility in terms of turn-around times.

2. RESPONSIBILITIES/SCOPE OF WORK

For this, under the direct supervision of the Activity Manager or the PPHF representative(s), the agency will be required to do the following:

• Take necessary briefs from the project team at PPHF

3. QUALIFICATION/CRITERIA FOR SELECTION:
The agency applying for this must have the following:
• Located/ work experience in Karnataka.
• Minimum 5 years experience working in supplying medical equipment to Govt. facilities like hospitals, PHC’s etc.
• Extensive experience in the maintenance of medical equipment.
• Local knowledge of culture and languages in Karnataka.
• Experience with similar assignments in Karnataka.
